d90345ebcd5411bd: PUTRAJAYA: Allegations of foreign interference aimed at toppling the Malaysian government must be investigated by the authorities rather than used as political fodder, as they involve national security and sovereignty.
Pakatan Harapan Wanita chief Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said such claims are extremely serious and, if true, should be formally reported to the relevant authorities for further action.

"If there truly were foreign attempts to bring down the Malaysian government, this is not something to boast about on the political stage. It is a matter that should be reported to the authorities because it touches on the nation's security and sovereignty," she said in a statement today.

Yesterday, the media reported claims by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang that a United States Embassy representative had once questioned him regarding the party's proposed candidate for prime minister.
Hadi claimed the meeting took place while Pas was still part of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition, around the time of the visit to Malaysia by then US President Barack Obama.
He made the claim during his closing address at the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar in Kota Baru yesterday.
The allegation prompted a response from the US Embassy, which denied ever attempting to determine Malaysia's political leadership and dismissed any claims to the contrary as false.
Aiman Athirah said the fact that the US Embassy had to issue a clarification over the matter was embarrassing for the country on the international stage.

She added that allegations involving foreign powers and domestic politics are no small matter, as they affect national sovereignty, the integrity of the democratic process, and the nation's political dignity.

"The question is, why make this statement now? What is the objective? Is it merely to build a narrative that certain parties were once 'victims of foreign interference', or does it open up a larger question as to why such a meeting occurred, what was discussed, and why it is only being revealed after more than a decade?" she said.
She stressed that the claims made by Hadi, along with the names of several individuals mentioned, must be investigated immediately to ascertain their validity.

"Haji Hadi's claim is very serious, and both he and the individuals he named must be investigated immediately. Is national security and sovereignty something that Pas can compromise on, or has compromised on all this while?

"Malaysian politics should not be built on conspiracy theories, perceptions, or half-baked accusations that could ultimately erode public trust in our democratic institutions and the nation," she said.
2fbadc9abaf785ed: LETTER: I know what it feels like to be inside a horrific road crash. I was seriously injured and trapped inside the wreckage, caused by a mechanical failure.
It took approximately four hours to rescue me, an eternity when you are trapped inside a mangled vehicle, injured, frightened and uncertain about what will happen next.
The firefighters worked tirelessly to get me out. The paramedics worked alongside them, doing everything they could to keep me safe.
Yet there is something about that day that still troubles me. I sometimes wonder whether someone took a photograph while i was trapped.

That is why i found Syed Mohammed Idid Syed Ahmed Idid's recent letter, "A man died. Why the laughing emoji?" particularly meaningful, reminding us that behind every road accident is a human life, and that ultimately, we all want to get home safely at the end of the day.
I would like to add another perspective to his message. Whenever an accident happens, many seem unable to resist becoming investigators and photographers.

People begin making assumptions about the driver, the vehicle and what must have happened. "He must have been speeding." "She must have been careless." "People who drive that type of car are always like this."
The question should be, "What happened in the moments before the crash, and what caused the chain of events?"
This distinction matters when considering the recent tragedy on the East Coast Expressway.

On Aug 31, an 11-vehicle collision near Lanchang, Temerloh claimed four lives, including Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, her husband Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, both 32, and their four-year-old son, Armaan Nazeef. Another victim was also killed, while three others were injured.
The circumstances and cause remain matters for the authorities to establish.
Nur Atiqah was the owner of Secangkir Cafe in Sungai Karang, Kuantan. Her family later decided that the cafe would operate for the final time on Sept 4.
They explained that they could not continue what she had created, particularly the cakes and recipes that were uniquely hers. That affected me deeply.
As a crash survivor, i have become more cautious about judging people involved in road accidents.
This is why i echo Syed Mohammed Idid's hope that we all get home safely at the end of the day.
We need a better road-safety culture. One that encourages people to stop and help rather than stop and photograph.
Perhaps that is the message we should carry forward from Syed Mohammed Idid's letter.
Stop treating tragedy as entertainment, speculation or an invitation to judge.
DR MARZIAH ZAHAR
Senior Lecturer
School of Business Management
Universiti Utara Malaysia

74117cd1d7b8e3d5: KUALA LUMPUR: AirAsia Group Bhd has clarified that its planned fundraising of up to RM4.74 billion (US$1.17 billion) is primarily aimed at refinancing and restructuring existing debt and consolidating its balance sheet, rather than funding operational shortfalls.
The group, formerly known As AirAsia X Bhd, said the fundraising comprises up to RM4.04 billion (US$1 billion) in international debt markets and RM700 million in local credit facilities.
AirAsia deputy group chief executive officer, Farouk Kamal said the fundraising is part of the group's efforts to optimise its balance sheet.
"Our current capital market initiatives represent a proactive balance sheet optimisation opportunity.
"We are leveraging our banking and financier relationships to systematically replace legacy, high-interest pandemic-era debt with streamlined, long-term facilities."
"This will optimise our capital structure, lower interest expenses, and build significant financial flexibility as we transition back into sustainable growth," he said in a statement.
AirAsia said the exercises are in line with its previous disclosures on capital structure optimisation.
The group raised about RM1.21 billion (US$300 million) in March this year amid global market escalations and fuel price volatility to extend debt tenures and reduce principal obligations.
"The primary objective of the funding strategy is to consolidate multiple existing facilities into a unified, lower-cost debt structure with extended maturities and better terms," AirAsia said.

The exercise would allow the group to refinance high-cost debt obligations incurred during the Covid-19 pandemic, lower its annual interest expenses, optimise non-fuel unit costs and secure liquidity for strategic working capital.

AirAsia had said when announcing its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 that it was in discussions with local and international financial institutions for up to RM4.04 billion (US$1 billion) in funding and RM700 million in local facilities, including plans for a targeted bond issuance.

For the quarter, the group recorded RM5.1 billion revenue, down one per cent year-on-year from the same quarter in 2025, despite an 11 per cent reduction in capacity as it prioritises yields over volume.
Revenue per available seat kilometre (RASK) rose 11 per cent year-on-year to 21.28 sen driven by fare adjustments and dynamic fuel surcharges.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) was down 56 per cent from the second quarter of 2025 at RM442.6 million despite a 58 per cent increase in fuel expenses as average jet fuel prices rose to about RM740 (US$183) per barrel.
AirAsia posted a net loss of RM830.5 million for the quarter. The group said it was heavily affected by foreign exchange movements.
"Excluding a forex loss of RM331 million, the group would have reported a net loss of RM499.6 million," AirAsia said in its second quarter 2026 financial results statement.
AirAsia said financial pressures during the quarter were largely concentrated in short-haul operations in Thailand, the Philippines and Indonesia as well as its long-haul operations in Malaysia.
Its core short-haul operations in Malaysia and Cambodia remained profitable.
The group said it has begun operational resets in the affected markets.

This included suspending underperforming long-haul routes, delaying the launch of its Bahrain hub and reducing fleet allocations in the Philippines and Indonesia to focus on high yield domestic and core Asean routes.
AirAsia also reduced its cost available seat kilometre (CASK) excluding fuel by seven per cent year-on-year to 11.02 sen during the second quarter 2026.
This is through measures such as freezing non-essential operational expenditure, optimising vendor structures and deferring uncommitted capital spending.
The group said it recovered about 70 per cent of higher fuel cost in the second quarter through dynamic fare adjustments and reductions in non-fuel unit costs.

It said average fares rose by over 20 per cent year-on-year across May and June after fare growth was limited to four per cent in April as much of its seat inventory had been sold before the geopolitical fuel price surge.

AirAsia also said it continues to implement a multi-layered risk management strategy to protect operating margins against fuel price volatility, which includes establishing a broader fuel hedging strategy across the group.
"Specifically for Thai AirAsia, the group has secured 13 per cent of its 3Q26 fuel consumption hedged at US$89 per barrel," the group said.
AirAsia also clarified that its planned 20-25 per cent capacity adjustment in the third quarter 2026 was a deliberate operational strategy aligned with seasonal travel patterns.
It said the third quarter historically represented the leanest period for regional air travel.
"The group will dynamically scale capacity back toward peak and pre-war levels in 4Q26 aligning with the strongest travel window of the year," it said.
Following the consolidation of its long-haul and short-haul operations under one group, AirAsia said it is now able to optimise aircraft allocation across its network more effectively.

This includes replacing wide-body Airbus A330 aircraft with narrow-body aircraft on routes such as Kuala Lumpur-Seoul and temporarily suspending certain routes including Kuala Lumpur to Sydney and Delhi.
"Complementing network changes, the strategic return of 25 older, less fuel-efficient aircraft during the period was negotiated on favourable commercial terms.
"This rightsizing eliminates fixed lease burdens and reduces non-fuel unit costs ahead of new aircraft deliveries scheduled for 2028 and beyond," AirAsia said.
Farouk said managing capacity during periods of weaker demand was part of the group's financial discipline.
"Managing capacity during low demand quarters is financial discipline expected of us.
"Rather than burning cash in a seasonally slower quarter, we chose to trim excess capacity, return older aircraft on favourable terms, and lower our overall lease obligations," he said.

90c9771f2f7cef5e: NANJIE (China): The crimson flags on Nanjie village's "East is Red" Square hang limp in the sweltering summer heat as a trickle of tourists take photos with a towering statue of Chairman Mao Zedong, still gleaming white almost 50 years after he died.
The Great Helmsman, who died on Sept 9, 1976, is still very much a fixture in central Henan province's Nanjie – often dubbed "China's last Maoist village".
Nostalgia for Mao's egalitarian ideals is growing in China as memories of his turbulent rule fade and the country grapples with a slowing economy and inequality.

Mao, who led the 1949 communist revolution against the ruling Nationalists, ushered in an era of collectivised ownership he argued would drive industry and unite the country, but his drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths.

While the ruling Chinese Communist Party maintains Mao was a revolutionary hero, it publicly acknowledged after his death that his devastating Cultural Revolution was a "grave mistake" – a verdict upheld by subsequent leaders.
In Nanjie, countless murals of the former Chinese leader are plastered around the village.
Residents still live under Maoist principles of shared ownership, while the rest of the country moved on from that economic model.
"I still revere him very much," Xie Kaiyue, a 22-year-old local university student, said of Mao, who died almost three decades before she was born.
"I think young people in the village and, actually, myself, aren't as strong-spirited as in the past... People were purer," she said.

Nearby, electric carts whisked visitors past uniform apartment blocks plastered with socialist slogans as guides explained how cooperative ownership in local enterprises funds free housing for residents.
Party line

Around 500 km north, in the mountain village of Dazhai in Shanxi province, once promoted by Mao as a national model after locals terraformed its arid hills into irrigated fields, tourists reminisce about an era when the Great Helmsman dominated political and social life.
"(People) didn't have enough to eat or to wear," Li, a 64-year-old tourist from Xi'an, said of his childhood.
"But... the whole country was full of vigour, and there was a spirit of struggling with heaven, earth, and people to change every aspect of China," the retiree said.
"Of course I miss it."
Now, Dazhai is overflowing with shops selling items that support Mao's personality cult – posters, playing cards and crockery emblazoned with his image, and the "Little Red Book" of his quotations.
Still, references to dark chapters of his decades in absolute power are tightly censored in public discourse.
The decade-long episode instigated by Mao in 1966 saw intellectuals brutally targeted as "class enemies" and schools shuttered, setting China back for years in education and development.

Private property and land were collectivised, while economic management pushed the country to the Great Famine, which the government says killed around 15 million people, while historians estimate around 20-43 million.
In one museum, text mentioning the Cultural Revolution had been crudely scraped off signage.

"Everything you see in the public domain... is the party line. No one is allowed to deviate from this," said scholar Xu Chenggang, who was targeted as a child in Beijing during the Cultural Revolution because his father was labelled a "rightist".
Mao's face is printed on banknotes, his portrait overlooks Tiananmen Square, and his body is preserved in a mausoleum.
Every year, new movies and TV shows dramatising Mao's life beam the message of his great deeds to the public.
Public discussion has been squeezed further under current leader Xi Jinping, who warns against "historical nihilism", or narratives contradicting the party's own.
"The Communist Party told people there were mistakes, but what's the meaning of 'mistake'? No one knows," Xu said.
'Great figure'
The sanitised history has left space for romanticised interpretations among youths frustrated by long working hours and intense competition in education and the job market.

In December, a viral video series on Bilibili – a platform popular with those under 30 – argued that the 2017 movie 'Youth', which follows young performers in a military dance troupe during the 1970s, was a subtle ode to the Cultural Revolution.
The videos, which praised Mao and blamed capitalist elites for crushing the movement, were removed after gaining more than 35 million views in less than a week.

"Today, there is more of a sense that the Cultural Revolution was a period of idealism, where society was fired by ideals and not by the relentless pursuit of money and material goods," said Kerry Brown, head of the Lau China Institute in London and author of a recent book on Mao.
"This is, of course, a total fabrication," he said.
Many also credit Mao with laying the foundation for China to become a modern, technologically advanced nation, said Mobo Gao, professor of Chinese studies at Adelaide University.
"They ask, where did (today's China) come from? It came from the establishment of the PRC," said Gao, who lived through the Mao era in rural Jiangxi province.
"Who was the one who really established the PRC? It must be Mao."
In Shijiazhuang, an industrial city of seven million northeast of Dazhai, 20-year-old Wang Zhihao and his classmates posed with a giant Mao statue opposite the municipal government.
"We admire and revere Chairman Mao very much. He is a great figure," Wang said, as the sound of elderly residents singing songs praising the Communist Party drifted over from the nearby square.
"He led the founding of New China."

95e8251b814d7f80: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — More than 600 Orang Asli children are now pursuing their studies at universities and colleges nationwide, reflecting a significant increase in the community’s participation in higher education and demonstrating the government’s concern for the group’s education.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the achievement was among the outcomes of the government’s emphasis on education as an important instrument to improve the social mobility of the Orang Asli community.

The Rural and Regional Development Minister said that when the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) was placed under his ministry four years ago, an initial target was set for 200 Orang Asli children to gain admission to higher education institutions.
“In the first year, the challenge was accepted. Not only did 200 enter university, but the number exceeded 300 Orang Asli who entered university that year.

“In the second year, I increased the target to 300. Clearly, the achievement of Orang Asli children entering university increased to 400 in the second year,” he said in his speech at the national-level Orang Asli Sports Carnival (KSOA) at EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Also present was Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Ahmad Zahid said the achievement of more than 600 students this year proved that the Orang Asli community had the ability to progress if given the appropriate educational opportunities and support.
“This represents good social mobility because education is an element that can improve the social status of any community in the world,” he said.

He said efforts to empower education among the Orang Asli community had also been expanded to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) through the provision of institutions specifically for the community.
Among them is the Paya Bungor Training Centre in Maran, Pahang, which currently has 135 Orang Asli students enrolled in TVET programmes offering both short- and long-term courses.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid also expressed his appreciation for the Johor government’s commitment in allocating RM600,000 to 60 Orang Asli villages in the state, amounting to RM10,000 for each village.
He also expressed hope that the allocation could be increased in the Johor Budget for next year.

Ahmad Zahid also expressed his appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for appointing former Skudai assemblywoman Marina Ibrahim as special officer in charge of Orang Asli affairs under the Sultan Ibrahim Foundation.
He said the appointment reflected His Majesty’s concern for the welfare and development of the Orang Asli community in Johor. — Bernama
f89ade598bd7030a: JERUSALEM, Sept 6 — The Israeli military said today it was carrying out strikes in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched drones at its soldiers, and urged residents of the town of Arab Salim to evacuate.

“Terrorists from the Hezbollah terrorist organisation launched two drones towards IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon,” the military said in a statement, adding that there were no reports of Israeli soldiers wounded.
“This constitutes a blatant violation by the Hezbollah terrorist organisation. In response, the IDF is now striking in southern Lebanon.”
In another message, the Israeli military warned residents of Arab Salim to leave ahead of imminent attacks.
“You are situated near a facility belonging to the terrorist organisation Hezbollah, against which the IDF will be operating,” it wrote in Arabic on Telegram.

Lebanon was drawn into the Middle East war in March after Iran-backed Hezbollah attacked Israel, which responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
Violence has lessened since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon later that month.
Israeli forces are operating inside a self-declared “security zone” around 10 kilometres (six miles) deep inside Lebanon along the border.
Authorities in Lebanon said yesterday that Israeli strikes killed four people in the country’s south and east. — AFP
55e5ecdb0676116a: KOTA KINABALU: Kuching City coach Aidil Sharin Sahak hailed striker Ajdin Mujagic's individual brilliance following a 2-0 Super League victory over Sabah FC at Likas Stadium on Saturday.
A brace from Mujagic, who scored two long-range goals in the fourth and 21st minutes, sealed all three points for the visitors.
Aidil said his team understood their responsibilities and executed the tactical plan effectively.
"I feel the players performed exceptionally well, from defending our goal to launching attacks.
"Every player delivered a strong performance, and I am delighted, especially after our disappointing 0-0 draw against Kelantan Red Warrior in the first leg of the FA Cup.
"Today was different. We came with strong determination and mindset, demonstrating clear improvement in the team," Aidil said at a post-match press conference.
He added that the victory served as a major boost ahead of their upcoming FA Cup round of 16 second-leg match against Kelantan.
"We rotated the squad slightly before coming here. The players gave their best, stuck to our strategy, and applied what they practised in training.
"The most important aspects were their work rate, commitment, and defensive discipline, which provide great motivation moving forward," said Aidil.
Meanwhile, Sabah coach Juan Torres Garrido attributed his side's defeat to individual errors and the opposition's individual quality.
Garrido said while defensive mistakes contributed to the outcome, the impact of Mujagic's two long-range strikes was unexpected.
"If a player scores two goals from 35 metres, it comes down to pure talent.
"We made mistakes and lost possession, though not near the penalty box. Today, they beat us because of one player's pure talent.
"The situation became much harder after those two goals, and we cannot always control that. They are a good team with good players, and good players do things like this," said Garrido.
Sabah will now prepare for their FA Cup round of 16 return-leg match against Selangor at MBPJ Stadium in Kelana Jaya on Wednesday.
Kuching remain second in the league with nine points, while Sabah are fourth on six.

91bafad4e5ab346a: LONDON, Sept 6 — A British-Nigerian influencer died after a penis enlargement procedure in Thailand allegedly triggered a fatal pulmonary embolism, according to a UK coroner’s report cited by the New York Post.
Igho “Tiny” Ubiribo, 43, was on holiday in Bangkok with his wife, Daniella Simba Allen, when he underwent the cosmetic procedure on March 5.
Details of his death only came to light yesterday, months after the procedure, with the New York Post reporting that a postmortem later linked the embolism to substances used in the injection.
Ubiribo had reportedly received injections containing hyaluronic acid and the local anaesthetic lidocaine.
Soon afterwards, while he and his wife were having a massage, he began complaining of chest pain and repeatedly lost consciousness, according to the report.
He was taken to Sukhumvit Hospital, where doctors found he was struggling to respond coherently to questions.
His condition rapidly deteriorated and he died from a pulmonary embolism before medical staff could carry out a CT scan to identify the cause.
Doctors reportedly performed CPR for more than 100 minutes in an attempt to save him.

A postmortem carried out under the authority of a UK coroner later concluded that the hyaluronic acid and lidocaine used during the procedure had caused the embolism, the New York Post reported, citing TMZ.

Hyaluronic acid fillers can be used in cosmetic procedures, including injections intended to temporarily increase penile girth. The effects typically last for several months and treatments can cost thousands of dollars.
Ubiribo had built a sizeable following online, with about 185,000 followers on Instagram, where he documented a lavish lifestyle.
According to the New York Post, he owned a US$1.1 million home in Los Angeles’ Crenshaw neighbourhood as well as a London apartment valued at about US$600,000.
He married Allen in an elaborate ceremony in Zimbabwe in 2022.
Following his death, Ubiribo was buried in London in a gold coffin reportedly costing more than US$700,000.
0f5320f5418afa23: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has dismissed claims that his relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has become strained.
Zahid said there were no issues between them, either personally or in their official capacity, including during cabinet meetings.
He said Barisan Nasional, as a component of the unity government, remained committed to maintaining political stability until the end of the current term.
"What is important for BN as a component of the unity government is political stability in the country until the end of the term.

"We make decisions and reach conclusions through a professional process," said Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, after officiating the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.
He said political stability was crucial to maintaining foreign investor confidence, attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) and supporting economic growth.
"We know that the Umno General Assembly resolution has determined that we remain in the unity government until the end of the term, and this is what we are doing to ensure political stability.
"This is to avoid any problems, particularly involving foreign investors and FDI, as well as to strengthen the country's economic growth," he said.

An international news portal recently quoted sources as claiming that relations between Anwar and Zahid had become strained over several issues, including BN's decision to contest against Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the recent Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
The report also claimed the alleged tension had resulted in recent cabinet meetings being shorter than usual.
1183d71529f6279b: KUALA LUMPUR: A team of United Sikhs Malaysia volunteers has met the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) and Wisma Putra officials in Kathmandu to coordinate flood relief efforts following their arrival yesterday.
The five-member Team A met the Malaysian officials at 6.20pm, with Smart focusing on locating missing Malaysians while the volunteers provide aid and temporary shelters to affected communities.
"We are coordinating with each other," United Sikhs Malaysia legal director Raspreet Kaur told the New Straits Times.
The team left today for Dhunche in Rasuwa district, about 120km north of Kathmandu, to establish a base camp. The journey is expected to take 10 to 12 hours.
From there, they will unload relief supplies before travelling off-road to Syapru Besi, about 40km from the Nepal-Tibet border.
Raspreet said the team's immediate priority was to build temporary shelters for affected families.
She said Nepalese local Raju Thapa had also sought assistance for 98 children whose parents remained missing.
The team will provide necessities, including colouring materials.
"The team remains focused on reaching the affected communities safely and providing practical assistance wherever possible," she said.
The volunteer group had earlier prepared mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 for some 300 affected families, with the supplies delivered to a gurdwara in Kathmandu.
Team A is expected to remain in Nepal for about two weeks, while other teams are on standby depending on needs on the ground.
Meanwhile, the Smart MAS01 contingent arrived in Kathmandu yesterday for its humanitarian and disaster relief mission after Nepal approved Malaysia's deployment.
The team brought 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including rescue and detection gear, communications systems, high-capacity drones, specialised tunnel rescue equipment and vehicles.
d2726cb1f0dc7b06: PUTRAJAYA: There is no need to call an early general election as long as Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim retains majority support in Parliament, says DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook.

Speaking to reporters after officiating at the DAP Wanita National Congress, Loke said the unity government was formed following an understanding reached after the 15th general election, with a five-year mandate.
He said there were still 15 months left in the current term, which should be used to implement reforms agreed upon by the Cabinet.
“For DAP, as long as the prime minister has majority support, there is no need to bow to any pressure to dissolve Parliament,” he said.

“So we will use these 15 months to implement all the reforms we agreed on, including some of the constitutional amendments approved by the Cabinet, such as the separation of the attorney-general and public prosecutor’s roles and a two-term limit for the prime minister.”

On Thursday, Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said it would be better for the next general election (GE16) to be held earlier than wait for Parliament to complete its term at the end of next year.
However, he said the Umno-led coalition was also prepared if the prime minister opted to see out his full five-year tenure.
Anwar said the proposal to hold GE16 earlier than scheduled can be considered, but the government is focussed on the economy, public wellbeing, and fighting corruption.
2769da623a484896: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has signalled that allocations for the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry could be increased, but added that public funds must be managed carefully and transparently.
Anwar said he had no objection to increasing the ministry's allocation as the funds would directly benefit farmers, padi growers, plantation operators and fishermen.
"I have no problem at all increasing aid allocations for the Agriculture Ministry because it will directly benefit farmers, padi growers, plantation operators and fishermen," he said.
However, he said that increased allocations must be accompanied by good governance to ensure the funds are used effectively.
198170167a12fd93: NEW YORK, Sept 6 — American teen Iva Jovic outlasted Philippines star Alexandra Eala in an epic three-hour showdown yesterday to reach the fourth round of the US Open, where fourth seed Coco Gauff awaits.
Jovic, the 14th seed, won five of the last six games for a 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 triumph over 17th-seed Eala after three hours and three minutes.
“That felt like a marathon and I felt like I lost my sanity five times over to win that match,” Jovic said. “But it’s really worth it for this feeling.”
Two of the top rising stars of women’s tennis made their Arthur Ashe Stadium debut a memorable battle that featured 17 service breaks in 33 games.
Jovic, 18 and Eala, 21, are friends and sometime doubles partners, knowing well each other’s skills and style. That helped produce seven service breaks in the first 11 games.
“I’m usually not one that shows that many emotions but this one really meant a lot to me. It’s everything to have another match here at the US Open,” said Jovic.
That match will be against compatriot Gauff, the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open champion.
“I’m going to be more than happy to just bring this fight and this energy and whatever happens I can leave with my head high,” Jovic said.
Jovic broke four times to win the first set but was broken three times by left-hander Eala to drop the second.
Eala broke Jovic in the first game of the third set when the American netted a backhand.
“I just tried to take my time in those moments and feel the energy and feel the crowd — even though they weren’t always rooting for me,” Jovic said.
Jovic smacked a forehand winner to break Eala in the fourth game and level the set, but the American double-faulted away a break in the fifth.
Jovic broke back to 4-4 with a backhand service return winner and broke again in the last game, smacking a forehand winner to reach match point and taking the victory when Eala netted a forehand.
Jovic, a quarter-finalist at this year’s Australian Open, won her first WTA title last year in Guadalajara at age 17. — AFP

9e82e4fbfbcf9f98: MIAMI: Lionel Messi set up both goals for Inter Miami as the MLS champions drew 2-2 with Atlanta United on Saturday in the Argentina star's first match since announcing his retirement from international football.

Thunderstorms and lightning delayed the start for 90 minutes, but there were sparks aplenty on the field after with Messi, Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer and most-capped player, at the heart of the action.
Miami grabbed the lead in the 32nd minute when Brazil's Casemiro rose to head home Messi's corner.
Atlanta equalised three minutes later when former Newcastle forward Miguel Almiron blasted home a low shot.
Former Liverpool and Barcelona star Luis Suarez put Miami into the lead with a measured finish on the cusp of half-time after a move down the left started by Messi.
But Swiss striker Breel Embolo struck home an 87th-minute penalty to secure a share of the spoils.
In Toronto, Derrick Etienne scored two minutes into second-half stoppage time to secure a dramatic 4-4 draw in a wild eight-goal thriller against Chicago.
Josh Sargent scored a hat-trick for Toronto, but Chicago's Maren Haile-Selassie scored twice before an own goal and Robert Lewandowski's 63rd minute strike put the visitors 4-3 up.
Philadelphia beat Montreal 2-0 as 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan scored in the 75th minute.
It gave the teenager four goals and seven assists this season, the most scoring contributions by a 16-year-old in a season, eclipsing the mark of 10 by Freddy Adu in 2005.

c7186b4361bdf652: SERDANG: The government should cancel the contracts of companies that repeatedly fail to fulfil their obligations to farmers and appoint new ones, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said agricultural assistance programmes should not be disrupted by repeated failures of companies entrusted to provide supplies or services.
"If a company like this repeatedly makes mistakes, cancel (the contract). Take a new company. Do not make farmers and padi growers the victims. Take action," he said.
He said the government needed to identify the companies involved, determine whether they had fulfilled their obligations and take appropriate action if they had failed to do so.
f6555ea7d8c631a1: SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to investigate delays in the distribution of fertiliser to padi farmers in Kedah.
Anwar said the delays had affected farmers, who had raised their concerns and submitted memoranda to him.
He said the government needed to determine the cause, including identifying the company entrusted with the distribution and whether it had fulfilled its obligations.

"We have to find out what the cause was. Which company was entrusted with it? Did they fulfil their promise or not? If they did not fulfil it, why was there no action against them?" he said at the closing of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 here today.
Also present were Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said enforcement action should be taken where necessary, including bringing those responsible to court or pursuing prosecution.
"If they need to be brought to court, bring them to court. If they need to be prosecuted, let MACC come in and investigate," he said.
Anwar said he had already instructed MACC to review the matter and the process involved.
"I have already asked MACC to come in and review the process. Do you know why? Because the Agriculture Ministry's record is good," he said.
He said delays in agricultural assistance were particularly serious as farmers and padi growers were already facing challenges, including weather and water-related problems.
"Do not let this become an issue that affects them further. They are already facing problems with the weather and water. This is something we cannot allow," he said.

In January, the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry was reported to be reviewing the subsidised fertiliser supply chain following complaints from farmers that delays had disrupted crop growth and increased their costs. https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/01/1350029/fertiliser-supply-delays-under-review-ministry-says

The ministry said short contract periods had previously caused supply disruptions when contracts expired before new suppliers were appointed. Procurement reforms, including longer contracts, have since been implemented to ensure continuity.

In August, the Kedah Darul Aman Information Secretariat reported that delays in subsidised fertiliser supplies, coupled with a nearly three-month vacancy in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) chairman's post, were disrupting padi cultivation and increasing pressure on farmers.

The secretariat quoted Kota Siputeh assemblyman Mohd Ashraf Mustaqim Badrul Munir as saying that as of June 29, only 37,560 bags of Additional Padi Compound Fertiliser 3 had been received, representing six per cent of the total requirement of 616,015 bags.
Only 30,799 bags had been distributed, leaving an estimated shortfall of 160,000 bags.
According to Agriculture Department guidelines, compound fertiliser should be applied 15 to 20 days after sowing, while urea is required around 25 to 40 days after sowing.
Additional compound fertiliser is applied during panicle initiation and flowering, depending on the maturity period of the padi variety.
119f348bf66fc5f8: PETALING JAYA: Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that his relationship with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has become increasingly strained, saying their ties remain cordial.
Zahid was responding to a Bloomberg report citing sources as saying that tensions between him and Anwar were worsening, with recent Cabinet meetings taking place for shorter periods than usual.
Zahid, who is the Umno president, also said his relationship with DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook remained very good.
“Cabinet meetings have been ending at 1pm as usual, not as reported.
“I sat next to him (Anwar), to the prime minister’s right. Loke, the transport minister, was also seated next to me,” he was quoted by Utusan Malaysia as saying.

Bloomberg reported that the tension between the prime minister and his deputy stemmed from Zahid’s decision for Barisan Nasional to contest against Pakatan Harapan in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.

The report also claimed that the situation was compounded by DAP’s pressure for institutional reforms to be implemented by year-end, while Anwar still needed BN’s support to secure a two-thirds majority in the Dewan Rakyat to pass constitutional amendments.
Zahid, however, said BN would continue to honour its pledge to remain in the unity government until the end of the current term.
“Umno is a party that keeps its promises. The decision was made to remain until the end of the 15th Parliament’s term.
“What is important is that we remain in the government, because that was the resolution unanimously adopted by Umno delegates at the previous general assembly,” he said.

Last month, former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said trust between Anwar and Zahid had hit its lowest point following BN’s decision to join forces with Perikatan Nasional for the Negeri Sembilan election.
Anwar brushed aside the claims and said that Khairy was only expressing his “personal view”.
432f261decc69f0a: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — DAP is pushing for two constitutional reform Bills covering the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the attorney general and public prosecutor to be brought back to the Dewan Rakyat when its next sitting begins on October 5.
DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said both draft Bills were ready and should be tabled during the sitting, which runs until December 8.
“The matter has been discussed and the drafts are ready. I have asked for both Bills to be tabled,” he was quoted by The New Straits Times as saying today.
According to Gobind, de facto Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said that the Bills were ready as part of the government’s institutional reform agenda.
The proposed prime ministerial term-limit amendment would cap a person’s tenure as prime minister at 10 years.
The measure narrowly failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Dewan Rakyat in March, receiving 146 votes in favour — two short of the 148 needed.

Following the defeat, Deputy Prime Minister II Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the government was confident of securing sufficient support when the Bill was retabled and that government MPs would support it.

Azalina said on September 3 that the Bill was now ready for its second reading, although its tabling and voting would be subject to the decision of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as leader of the House.
She also said the constitutional amendments would require a two-thirds majority.
Gobind said the term-limit proposal should be refined before its second reading.
The other reform would separate the attorney general’s role as the government’s legal adviser from that of the public prosecutor, who oversees criminal prosecutions.
The proposed separation was referred to a parliamentary special select committee for further scrutiny after being tabled earlier this year, with the draft subsequently revised.
Azalina said the revised proposal was also ready for Parliament and that the changes included a greater role for Parliament in scrutinising the appointment of the public prosecutor.

Gobind also said DAP had also raised the vacant attorney general’s post and equal allocations for elected representatives at its central executive committee meeting, with both matters to be brought to the central Pakatan Harapan leadership.
“We hope the appointment process can be completed as soon as possible, including taking into account the views of the public and opposition MPs,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the appointment of the attorney general and public prosecutor should be free from political discrimination.
“We respect the mandate given to every elected representative,” he added.
5ded764f64e04cd8: SINGAPORE, Sept 6 — American eggs are back on Singapore supermarket shelves after more than 20 years — although shoppers will have to pay a premium.
Eggs from US brand Contented Hen are now being sold at more than 50 FairPrice outlets, as importers seek to widen distribution following the resumption of US egg exports to Singapore in July.
The eggs, sourced from pasture-raised and free-range hens on farms in the US Midwest, are available at 43 FairPrice Finest stores and eight FairPrice hypermarkets, The Straits Times reported.
A dozen free-range white or brown eggs costs S$12.80 (RM40.80), while 12 organic free-range eggs are priced at S$14.80.
That is considerably more than mainstream eggs from Singapore and Malaysia, which typically cost between S$2.85 and S$4.55 for 10 at FairPrice.
But the supermarket group says the arrival of US eggs gives Singapore another supply source as the country strengthens its food resilience.

“Eggs are an essential source of protein. The introduction of US eggs further enhances our food supply resilience,” Leroy Seow, FairPrice Group’s managing director for products, told The Straits Times.
“Ultimately, expanding our sourcing network ensures daily essentials remain available, accessible and within reach for all in Singapore,” he added.
FairPrice currently sources eggs from 10 markets, including Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and the US.
US producers stopped selling eggs to Singapore in the early 2000s after the Republic tightened import requirements.
That changed earlier this year when US agricultural officials and the Singapore Food Agency reached agreement on export certification standards and systems for tracing eggs during disease outbreaks.
For now, however, the American imports are more likely to compete at the premium end of the market than replace everyday eggs from Singapore or Malaysia.
Yukako Matsuka, director at Singapore-based consulting firm YCP, said Contented Hen’s organic eggs, at about S$1.23 each, were cheaper than some organic options from Australia and New Zealand.
“At this price point, US eggs are better viewed as an additional premium choice rather than a mass-market substitute for regular eggs,” she said.
“Demand is therefore likely to develop gradually among consumers who place greater value on animal welfare, organic certification and traceability.”
Some shoppers are already taking notice.
Homemaker Ashley Lee, 44, swapped a S$19.80 carton of Australian organic eggs for the American option on September 5.
“It’s a lot cheaper,” she told The Straits Times. “I pay a lot of attention to where my food comes from and what the chickens are fed.”
Software engineer Cindy Ong, 30, was less convinced, saying she would probably buy the US eggs only on promotion.
“It’s a bit expensive,” she said.
Contented Hen eggs are being imported by N&N Agriculture under a long-term agreement to supply FairPrice.
More US eggs could soon follow, with another Singapore importer, Kai Young Huat, in talks to supply eggs from a separate American farm to FairPrice and Sheng Siong.
Representatives from eight US egg producers also visited Singapore earlier this month to meet importers, retailers and food manufacturers.
Sean Delano, executive director of business development at Mid-States Specialty Eggs, said its eggs take about 20 to 24 days to reach Singapore by sea.
“It takes a little longer to get here, but they are refrigerated, so the quality stays,” he said.
“We can still provide a fresh egg because it’s under that refrigeration while it travels.”
Singapore’s egg supply exceeded 2.2 billion in 2025, with Malaysia remaining its biggest overseas supplier.
Local farms currently meet less than 35 per cent of Singapore’s egg demand, underscoring the value of adding more overseas sources.
b3fc9b48e6ef7e96: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been urged not to bow to calls for an early dissolution of Parliament to pave the way for the 16th General Election (GE16).

DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said this was in line with the party's position that Anwar should continue to lead the Madani government as long as the Tambun MP commands a majority in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said Anwar should use the remaining 15 months to implement various reforms and the government's shared agenda before the 15th Parliament's term ends in December 2027.
"After the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections, we have heard many calls from various parties and quarters urging the prime minister to dissolve Parliament to pave the way for GE16.
"Our position is that as long as Anwar has a majority in the Dewan Rakyat, there is no need to bow to any pressure to hold GE16.

"We also urge, hope and support Anwar, as Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, to continue leading the government until the end of the 15th Parliament's term," he said when officiating the DAP Women's Congress in Putrajaya today.
Also present were DAP Wanita chief and deputy chairman Teo Nie Ching, her deputy Yeoh Bee Yin, and DAP Wanita vice-chiefs Yeong Syefura Othman and P. Kasturiraani.
96c578cc08f07ef3: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia is seen as having little urgency to adjust its monetary policy stance with inflation remaining well contained despite stronger economic growth and emerging cost pressures.
The central bank is therefore expected to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent through 2026.
Bank Negara's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) kept the OPR unchanged at 2.75 per cent at its September 2026 meeting, in line with market expectations.

Kenanga Research said the MPC's latest policy statement remained largely unchanged, maintaining that the current policy stance was "consistent with the outlook of continued price stability and sustainable economic growth".

The MPC also retained its forward guidance that it would "remain vigilant to ongoing developments and assess the balance of risks surrounding the outlook for domestic inflation and growth", reinforcing Bank Negara's data-dependent approach.

Kenanga Research noted that the central bank had adopted a more constructive assessment of global and domestic growth prospects, with global growth supported by strong technology expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.
Bank Negara now expects the economy to grow by around 5.0 per cent in 2026, compared with its previous guidance that growth would remain firmly within the 4.0 per cent to 5.0 per cent range.

For 2027, the central bank expects growth to remain resilient, supported by electrical and electronics (E&E) exports, continued strength in technology-related non-E&E exports, sustained tourism spending, stable labour market conditions and ongoing investment activity.
Kenanga Research said inflation remained well contained, with headline and core inflation averaging 1.8 per cent and 2.0 per cent respectively in the first seven months of 2026.

Despite elevated costs and robust growth, the MPC noted limited pass-through to consumer prices, supported by domestic policy measures, stable demand conditions and limited spillovers from export-led growth into wages.
"Still, Bank Negara flagged risks from the Middle East conflict, with elevated global commodity prices posing upside risks to domestic costs," it added.
The firm maintained its call for the OPR to stay at 2.75 per cent through 2026, saying the current stance balances firmer growth momentum with emerging external cost pressures.

"With growth now assessed at around 5.0 per cent in 2026 and inflation (July: 1.8 per cent) well below levels that would warrant tightening, there is limited urgency for further policy adjustment," it said.

Kenanga Research also forecasts Malaysia's 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 5.3 per cent, up from 5.2 per cent in 2025, following stronger-than-expected first-half performance supported by net exports and resilient domestic demand.
Meanwhile, MBSB Research said the latest policy statement reflected a more confirmed view of economic strength while highlighting concerns over persistent cost-push inflation.
"This supports our view of a prolonged rate pause, keeping the OPR steady at 2.75 per cent for the foreseeable future," it said.

On the global front, MBSB Research said Bank Negara viewed global headline inflation as having eased in recent months, although price pressures were expected to remain sticky as earlier energy cost increases gradually filter through to consumer prices.
Geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East remained a risk to global GDP growth and could sustain upward cost pressures.
Resilient capital allocation across the global technology sector continued to provide a buffer against broader macroeconomic weakness, it said.

However, elevated global borrowing costs could temper the sector's growth prospects, while prolonged geopolitical tensions, tighter global financial conditions and elevated financial market valuations posed additional downside risks.
MBSB Research said Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026, supported by robust exports and solid domestic consumption.
It said key growth catalysts include strong demand for E&E and technology-related non-E&E exports, the ongoing recovery in foreign tourist arrivals and healthy domestic spending.

Stable market conditions and ongoing investment activity are also expected to support domestic demand, although prolonged conflict in the Middle East and lower commodity production could pose downside risks.
On inflation, MBSB Research said Bank Negara viewed consumer price pressures as well anchored despite elevated costs and robust GDP growth.
The limited pass-through to retail prices reflected the combined impact of domestic price controls, stable consumer demand and constrained wage growth, it said.
MBSB Research reaffirmed its expectation of an extended OPR hold through 2026 and raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.1 per cent from 4.5 per cent previously.
The upgrade reflected stronger-than-expected first-half momentum, driven by a recent surge in export performance and steady domestic demand, it said.
Its macro outlook assumes that the worst of the Middle East conflict has passed, mitigating severe downside risks to supply chains.

MBSB Research continues to expect inflation to rise to 2.0 per cent in 2026 from 1.4 per cent in 2025, mainly due to supply-driven pressures that are expected to be mitigated by ongoing policy measures.

It said downside risks included heightened geopolitical tensions, higher US tariffs, prolonged elevated global bond yields and a potential expansion of tariffs on the semiconductor industry, which could disrupt Malaysia's technology sector and broader economic outlook.

66a293cf4e45e1a6: NEW YORK: World number two Elena Rybakina avenged her French Open defeat to Yuliia Starodubtseva on Saturday, beating the unseeded Ukrainian 7-6 (8/6), 6-3 to reach the US Open last 16.

The hard-hitting Kazakh, who claimed her second Grand Slam title at the Australian Open in January, fell to Starodubtseva in the second round at Roland Garros, a defeat that may have been on her mind as she struggled to find her rhythm in the opening set.
Starodubtseva took full advantage of Rybakina's struggles with her forehand and broke for a 5-4 lead.
But Rybakina steadied, breaking back with an angled drop shot to level the set.
She saved a set point in the tiebreaker with one of her 12 aces, and with the first set in hand attacked in the second with confidence.
A double fault from Starodubtseva handed Rybakina a break to open the second and Rybakina maintained the edge to finish the job in just under two hours.
"It was a tough match," Rybakina said. "I feel like it wasn't my best performance, but Yuliia she's a great player. Last time we had a battle, too, and I'm glad I could win in straight sets."
Rybakina now just needs two wins -- to reach the semi-finals -- to be assured of supplanting Aryna Sabalenka atop the world rankings -- even if Sabalenka wins a third straight US Open title.
"Not there yet," she said. "It's still very far. I need to focus on my next match and not think about it."
That next match will be against four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka, who beat Elise Mertens of Belgium 6-3, 3-6, 7-5.
97aec1a9912931e3: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez is planning a farewell match featuring both Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in the same team at Boca Juniors' La Bombonera Stadium.
The event is set for December as Tevez seeks a proper send-off at the club where he won 11 titles, including five Primera Division championships.
Tevez, who retired in June 2022, has consulted former teammate and current Boca Juniors president Juan Roman Riquelme about scheduling the match for Dec 12-13 or the following weekend.
The aim is to assemble a team of friends from a career that included stints at Manchester United, Manchester City, and Juventus.
More than 60 stars who shared the pitch with Tevez are expected to take part.
The headline names are Messi and Ronaldo, with both rumoured to be involved in a rare moment playing on the same side.
The two stars only played against each other during their careers, primarily at Barcelona and Real Madrid.
Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors, left for Europe, and returned twice, remaining one of the most popular figures in the club's modern history.
5e740072327ff7f4: KUALA LUMPUR: GTA Holdings Bhd (GTA), a provider of aviation maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services, intends to establish a Centre of Excellence (CoE) after its listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia.
This new facility aims to enhance its research and development (R&D), training, and technological capabilities within the MRO sector.

Its managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Nonee Ashirin Mohd Radzi said the post-listing development plan would enable GTA to position itself as a key industry player supported by its original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners, while contributing towards Malaysia's self-reliance in the defence industry.

"The CoE will allow us to position ourselves as a key player in research and technology, with the backing of our OEM partners. We are going to invest in a new facility that will perhaps include R&D and training programmes, within which there will be a CoE.

"The plan is part of our National Defence Industry Policy (NDIP), as we are encouraged to have greater self-reliance through the development of local capabilities and technology transfer," she told Bernama in an exclusive interview recently.
Nonee Ashirin said the company is exploring investment in a Level 4 test bench and the necessary equipment, including the Hydromechanical Unit (HMU).
The HMU is a component of the helicopter engine that regulates the flow of oil into the turbine.
"The HMU is a highly specialised capability that is typically retained by OEMs, as they are generally reluctant to transfer this expertise to third parties.
"However, we are currently in negotiations and, hopefully, we will be able to proceed with the investment. I cannot disclose the cost at this stage as discussions are still ongoing," she said.
Strengthening Relations with MINDEF, Defence Sector

Nonee Ashirin emphasised that GTA remained committed to strengthening its core capabilities in the MRO sector, developing additional areas, such as landing gear, wheels and brakes, mainly by maintaining a good relationship with the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF).
She emphasised that GTA has over a decade of experience serving MINDEF and establishing trust with the Malaysian Armed Forces.

"We are well positioned as such because of the trust we have built with our customers over the years. The OEM understands that we have a very good relationship and that we have built up the technical expertise. So, we have become the sole provider for the OEM in Malaysia.

"We are also investing in increasing our human capital development. This will further strengthen our ability to support the operational requirements of our customers as Malaysia's aerospace and defence needs to evolve," said Nonee Ashirin.
Brunei MRO expansion
On regional expansion, Nonee Ashirin said the company has secured its position as distributor in Brunei, engaging primarily with the Royal Brunei Air Force.
"The Royal Brunei Air Force operates six helicopters, with each helicopter powered by two engines, which means there are 12 engines in Brunei that we will be looking to support," she said.
GTA is slated for listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Sept 8, 2026, and aims to raise RM71.75 million from its initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO comprises the issuance of 329 million shares in GTA, consisting of a public issue of 205 million new ordinary shares and 124 million existing shares at an issue price of 35 sen per share.
With an enlarged share capital of 1.29 billion shares, GTA's total market capitalisation upon listing is expected to be approximately RM451.97 million.

2ffec1d19bc2e2f7: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's strong economic fundamentals will continue to support investment opportunities across its capital markets, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said.
He said Malaysia's economic model also emphasised strong governance, providing Malaysians with greater opportunities to invest.

However, investor education and improved financial literacy were critical to ensuring Malaysians could make informed investment decisions based on their personal circumstances, investment objectives and risk appetite, he said.
"I think the importance of avoiding financial scams is really becoming a real social issue, particularly here in Malaysia.

"We wouldn't know what's too good to be true if we do not have the set levels of financial literacy and investor education to differentiate between what's a credible investment proposition and what is really completely unrealistic or illusive," he said in his keynote remarks at the opening ceremony of the InvestSmart X Bursa Marketplace Fair 2026.
Johan said the scale of investment scams in Malaysia was alarming, with Malaysians losing approximately RM1.47 billion to such scams in 2025.
He said he hoped the InvestSmart X Bursa Marketplace Fair 2026 would help Malaysians make more informed investment decisions and better protect themselves against scams.

Investment opportunities in the Malaysian market remained attractive, with the capital market offering various options through fund managers and brokers to cater to different investment objectives and risk profiles, he added.
The Securities Commission Malaysia and Bursa Malaysia collaborated on the InvestSmart initiative, held on Sept 5 - 6.

The inaugural collaboration combines investor education, market insights and practical guidance, and is intended to better equip participants with the knowledge to evaluate investment opportunities, understand risks and identify potential scams.
0b213b71b9311e2f: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has been actively laying the groundwork to pave the way for a possible nuclear application in the country's energy mix, although it may not materialise in the foreseeable future.

The big question is, who will spur the civil nuclear project in the country -- private firms or government-related energy giants like Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) or Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), which are said to be keen to undertake the massive development.

With the war between the United States and Iran continuing, disrupting the whole West Asia region and globally, Malaysia has seriously considered alternatives and examined many countries' energy initiatives, including the deployment of civil nuclear applications for industrial and general use.

Just last week, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) shared at a national workshop organised here that focused on human resource development modelling, a strategy that supports workforce planning by projecting future staffing needs, as the country looks to build capacity to support current and future nuclear applications.

In March this year, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof was quoted as saying that Malaysia has undertaken a comprehensive assessment of its potential nuclear energy programme, covering policy development, regulatory frameworks, project feasibility, industry participation, stakeholder engagement and human capital development.

Fadillah, who is also the Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), said the move to explore nuclear energy for electricity generation is a strategic effort to strengthen long-term energy security while supporting the country's clean energy transition.

Previously, Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI) Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang stated that Malaysia is actively exploring nuclear energy for future electricity generation under a structured framework with PETRA, with key nuclear initiatives led by MOSTI.

Led by Chang, the ministry launched the National Nuclear Technology Policy (DTNN) 2030 to promote peaceful applications of nuclear technology. The minister said a government-commissioned pre-feasibility study on the use of nuclear energy has found promising potential for its adoption as a clean, stable and reliable energy source for Malaysia's long-term energy security.

Juwai IQI global chief economist Shan Saeed said Malaysia's evaluation of civil nuclear energy is strategically sound and economically timely. He said under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), nuclear power is being assessed as a low-carbon component of the country's future electricity architecture, with MyPOWER Corporation coordinating a feasibility process aligned with the IAEA's Milestones Approach.
"The 13MP sets an initial operational ambition of 2031, although deployment must remain conditional on safety, regulatory readiness and commercial viability," he told Bernama here recently.
AI, Data Centre Boom Boost Energy Demand

The booming of data centres across the Asean region, which has seen Malaysia leading the growth, strengthens the economic case. Apart from that, Malaysia is also aggressive in driving its artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives toward becoming an AI Nation by 2030.

The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) approved RM144.4 billion in data-centre and cloud-computing investments between 2021 and mid-2025. By mid-August 2025, TNB had secured electricity-supply agreements for 47 data-centre projects with maximum demand of 6.7 gigawatts (GW).
MIDA also projected data-centre power demand could exceed 5GW by 2035 - equivalent to about 18 per cent of Peninsular Malaysia's 2025 installed capacity.
Shan said reliable electricity is therefore moving from an infrastructure consideration to a national competitiveness imperative.

"The gains would extend beyond data centres to semiconductor fabrication, electrical and electronics manufacturing, chemicals, advanced materials and green hydrogen. Nuclear could complement Malaysia's renewable-energy base with firm generation when solar output fluctuates, while diversifying the power mix and reducing exposure to imported-fuel volatility," said the economist.

McKinsey estimated that the US data-centre demand could rise from 25GW in 2024 to more than 80GW by 2030. ExxonMobil projects global electricity demand will expand by approximately 70 per cent by 2050.
"The competitive frontier is shifting from land, tax incentives and connectivity towards dependable, scalable power. Technological prudence remains essential," Shan said.
Tapping the Strength of Petronas, TNB
With the government laying the groundwork, Petronas and TNB will likely lead the commercial initiatives, based on their strength and capacity.

Shan said ideally the optimal model would be government-led but commercially disciplined. He advised that the Malaysia Programme Office for Power Electricity Reform Corporation (MyPOWER) should remain the programme coordinator, supported by the Energy Commission, Department of Atomic Energy Malaysia (Atom Malaysia) and the Malaysian Nuclear Agency.

"TNB is the natural domestic anchor for system planning and grid integration; Petronas could contribute expertise in complex-project delivery, safety management, international procurement and capital deployment. Experienced international vendors would initially provide reactor technology and operating expertise, while hyperscalers could strengthen project bankability through long-term power-purchase agreements," he added.
Finding the Perfect Fit for Malaysia
Apart from capacity building, the most important task is finding a suitable nuclear application to fulfil the country's energy needs.

On July 10, 2025, Malaysia signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation with the United States, which supports the former's broader clean energy exploration and long-term energy security. It also engaged in partnership networks with China and Russia to enhance its preparedness for a future nuclear energy programme that is safe, well-regulated and strategically planned.
Petronas and TNB are believed to be looking at some civil nuclear options, including third-generation nuclear fission.

"Insofar as the kind of technologies that we (Malaysia) are considering, whether it is from Korean or Russian or American or British or French, we kind of have to be a little bit more agnostic because we need to find the one that is fit for purpose in this region. Now, people have been saying the Americans and the Russians have got a bit of a lead because, think about it, aircraft carriers carry nuclear reactors at risk. So it's already a floating solution.

"I think we need to consider all the attributes of what makes it secure. This is another one where you have to make sure you can take on the cost of delivering nuclear energy because it's super expensive to build. Once built, the ongoing operating expenditure (opex) is very low," said a source close to the deal.
Among other options, Malaysia is also looking at Canada, which is currently implementing small modular reactors (SMRs), which, among others, are said to be suitable for deployment to data centres.
Through its SMR Action Plan, Canada is advancing its nuclear application and benefiting Canadians in many ways.

Apart from that, there is also the possibility of looking at floating power units (FPUs), which are said to be well-suited for coastal nations, the source said, citing Rosatom, the Russian state corporation leading in nuclear energy, nuclear non-energy goods and high-tech products.
Whatever the options - from SMRs or FPUs to third-generation nuclear fission - many factors need to be considered as Malaysia aims to make nuclear energy part of the generation mix by 2031.
What is the Ideal Timeline?

Shan said ideally, if the first power could come around between 2038 and 2042, it would be credible. "The strategy is about turning ambition into architecture. Compute capacity ultimately depends upon energy capacity. Build institutions first, contracts second and concrete last," he added.

Shan cited Wood Mackenzie, which models Malaysian SMR deployment from 2035, reaching 1.2GW by 2050. "The 2026–2030 period should prioritise legislation, workforce development, site evaluation, independent regulation, financing, waste management and ring-fenced decommissioning provisions," he added.

d7bfd675a3568854: SHENZHEN, Sept 6 — Chinese electric vehicle (EV) giant BYD Co Ltd is expected to announce within a week its next move for further expansion in Malaysia, amid questions over whether the automaker will collaborate with a local partner or establish its own manufacturing facility.
BYD vice-president Liu Xueliang said the company would continue exploring cooperation with local partners to support the development of Malaysia’s new energy vehicle (NEV) industry.

“We will continue to explore, together with local partners, how we can better support the development of Malaysia’s new energy vehicle industry. Of course, our development in Malaysia has also been progressing very well. Very soon, we will announce our approach towards sustainable development,” he told Malaysian media after the Asia-Pacific Story session titled “Stories of Industrial Integration” here yesterday.
Asked whether BYD would pursue cooperation with a local partner or opt for another approach, Liu remained tight-lipped, saying: “Wait another week and we will announce it.”
The remarks come amid heightened interest in BYD’s next move in Malaysia, particularly over its local manufacturing strategy and potential partnerships.
BYD’s plans have attracted attention as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its EV ecosystem while encouraging greater localisation and investment across the automotive supply chain.

In May, it was reported that BYD was evaluating a potential contract assembly partnership with Sime Motors’ Inokom plant in Kulim, Kedah, as the Chinese automaker reviewed its local manufacturing strategy in Malaysia.

Progress on BYD’s proposed manufacturing plant in Tanjung Malim, Perak, appeared to have stalled as of March this year. This was followed by a statement from the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) addressing claims circulating on social media regarding conditions imposed on BYD’s manufacturing licence and other related policies.

Meanwhile, beginning July 1 this year, fully imported or completely built-up (CBU) EVs are required to have a minimum declared cost, insurance and freight (CIF) value of RM200,000, as well as a minimum power output of 245 horsepower (180 kilowatts).

Liu said BYD has reaffirmed its commitment to long-term investment in Malaysia despite developments that have affected the progress of its plans, while identifying east Malaysia as a market with significant growth potential.

“We believe east Malaysia still has significant room for development, but first, we hope to have suitable models for the east Malaysian market,” he added.

bfdce3ac86d9c7bc: Kehebatan Tun M dalam politik memang tidak ada siapa yang boleh tandingi. Sama ada beliau berkuasa atau tidak, gelagat dan kata dua beliau akan sering menjadi buah mulut rakyat sekalian. Itu hebatnya Mahathir.

Beliau tidak perlu guna ayat al-Quran langsung dan tidak perlu ceramah berjela-jela dalam Facebook, cuma datang, duduk atas kerusi roda dan senyum sambil melambai. Itu pun sudah cukup untuk memulakan ribut taufan bersama halilintar.

Kenapa Tun M tak dijemput secara rasmi, 'sound' beberapa influencer yang becok berceloteh. Inikan suatu ketidakadilan kepada seorang tokoh negara? Sebenarnya saya pun agak setuju dengan teguran ini tetapi ada lima perkara yang perlu kita semua renungi dahulu.

Perkara pertama adalah apa yang disebut oleh Rafizi dalam podcastnya bila ditanya tentang isu ini. Saya berterima kasih dengan Rafizi yang memberi maklumat yang kita semua pun tak tahu. Kata Rafizi, Tun M sendiri yang mengubah protokol menjemput bekas perdana menteri untuk majlis penting seperti merdeka pada 2018.

Rafizi memberi alasan takkanlah Tun M nak duduk sebelah seorang penjenayah dan seteru beliau. Tetapi ada influencer yang tegur, Najib belum penjenayah lagi sebab baru buka kes. So, what’s the problem? Yang penting, seperti biasa, Tun memang bijak baling batu dan sembunyi tangan sambil senyum dan melambai.

Perkara kedua, kalaulah kita ada protokol untuk menjemput bekas perdana menteri atau kita ikut adab Melayu lah untuk jemput orang besar-besar, I must assume yang protokol tu dibuat dengan anggapan bahawa bekas perdana menteri tidak lagi berpolitik.

Dalam kes Tun M, beliau masih giat berpolitik dan rasanya sanggup memegang tampuk kerajaan sebagai PM untuk kali ketiga! Jadi, kalau begini rupanya, patutkah PM sedia ada menjemput seterunya dalam politik ke pentas Merdeka?

Perkara ketiga pula adalah Tun M telah membuat naratif bahawa Melayu akan hilang kuasa kalau tidak duduk di bawah satu payung besar. Sudah tentulah, payung tu dia yang punya. Jadi kalau semua Melayu duduk di situ kita boleh teka tiga kali siapa akan jadi PM.

Namun demikian, apa yang saya gusarkan adalah dengan membina naratif ini maka ia membuat suatu permusuhan dengan rakyat lain bukan Melayu termasuk Bumiputra semua. Patutkah seorang bekas PM yang menerajui negara dua kali dan masih membina naratif permusuhan antara Melayu dan bukan Melayu dijemput ke pentas duduk bersama parti PH yang tidak pernah menggunakan ras atau isu perkauman?
Saya pun tidak tergamak untuk duduk sebelah orang sebegini, tidak kisah lah dia PM berapa kali pun. Orang yang membuat kita bermusuh-musuh, bagi saya batang tubuh itu lah musuh terbesar negara kita.

Nasib baik Tun M tidak jadi seperti seorang guru agama yang nak buat kita bermusuh antara orang Islam dan bukan Islam, yang itu lagi ‘haru’ kata orang utara. Saya rasa Tun M baik sikit daripada tok guru agama yang pandai tafsir Quran ikut suka dia.

Perkara keempat adalah Tun M telah pernah membuat naratif Malaysia ini bukan negara multicultural sebab tidak ada disebutkan dalam konsep Malaysia secara undang-undang. Sekali lagi beliau memainkan isu ‘pendatang’ dan memainkan lagu lama bahawa pendatang akan take over everything kalau Melayu tak sedar dan tak bersatu. Same old song but very efective still.

Maklumlah orang Melayu ramai tidak belajar falsafah dan sejarah peradaban dunia. Kebanyakan Melayu belajar kejuruteraan, seni bina, perubatan, undang-undang dan bila pencen baru mengadap kuliah agama.

Mahathir adalah seorang pembaca tegar dan dia faham selok belok sejarah Malaysia dan dunia. Sejarah subjek kegemarannya, saya baca dalam buku beliau A Doctor in the House. Saya memang baca banyak buku Tun M, saya rasa empat buah kesemuanya. Jadi, kita kena tanya diri kita sebagai rakyat, do we want someone yang tidak admit kita negara multicultural?

Perkara kelima, memanglah dari satu sudut, kita patut jemput orang tua itu. Memang kita patut honor seorang pemimpin seperti Tun M. Tetapi jika batang tubuh itu sendiri bergerak untuk mengkucar-kacirkan kita semua, what should we do?

Pada 2016, Tun M berkempen untuk menyelamatkan Malaysia daripada perompak 1MDB. Beliau ke hulu dan ke hilir menjaja Malaysia bakal bankrap dengan si perompak ini. Bagi saya, we owe Tun M a debt of gratitude sebab dengan kempen itu kita rakyat dapat menumbangkan Umno sebagai gergasi berkuasa.

Dalam bab itu, Tun M memainkan peranan kita sebagai a united rakyat to save our country. Tetapi apabila beliau memainkan sentimen perkauman untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan perpaduan, that is an entirely different matter.

Maka itu, kita kena renung sendiri sama ada kita nak bagi hormat atau tidak kepada orang seperti Tun M. Saya sendiri amat menghormati beliau dalam banyak perkara seperti ketegasan beliau tentang ekstremis agama, tentang menimba ilmu dan memahirkan diri dalam sains, teknologi dan Bahasa Inggeris.

Tetapi saya tidak akan berkompromi kepada sesiapa pun yang cuba menjurangkan hubungan baik kita sebagai rakyat Malaysia dengan meniup bahang kaum, agama atau sejarah.That is the line I will not allow anyone to cross.
Itu jalur pemisah antara Merdeka sebagai rakyat dengan mereka yang nak menjatuhkan idea negara-bangsa kita.
