2a1ccd068369a150: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 —Malaysia’s representative Taanusiya Chetty matched the country’s best-ever result at the Miss World pageant 28 years ago by finishing third in the 2026 final in Nha Trang, Vietnam, last night.
Joheirry Mola Dominguez of the Dominican Republic was crowned Miss World 2026, while Elisabeth Reynes Alabern of Spain finished second.

Taanusiya, 26, finished among the top three after delivering impressive and consistent performances throughout the nearly month-long competition, overcoming the challenge of 110 other contestants from around the world.

The achievement matches the record set by Lina Teoh, who also finished third at Miss World 1998, making the two Malaysian representatives the country’s best-performing contestants in the history of the contest.

Apart from Teoh, other Malaysian representatives who previously recorded strong results include Rahimah Orchient Yayah, who advanced to the Top 10 in 1994, while Deborah Henry made it to the Top 16 in 2007.
Taanusiya, better known as Taanu, qualified for the Top Six after winning the Beauty With A Purpose (BWAP) segment, edging out Zimbabwe’s Brunette Makanyiso.
BWAP is one of the major Miss World recognitions, awarded based on the contestants’ commitment to and impact of the community projects they champion.
Meanwhile, during the evening gown segment, the Miss World Malaysia 2024/2025 titleholder looked elegant in a pink gown by Vietnamese fashion designer Minh Tuan Couture.
Throughout the competition, Taanusiya attracted attention with her confidence, personality and impressive performances in several segments before securing a place on the podium.
She also captured public attention after a video of her speaking in four languages - English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil - during the Miss World 2026 Head-to-Head Challenge on Aug 23 went viral.
The achievement not only brings pride to Malaysia on the international stage, but also establishes Taanusiya as one of the emerging figures in the global beauty pageant scene. — Bernama
a177cbb67b0038bd: KUALA LUMPUR: Terengganu coach Nafuzi Zain could not hide his disappointment after his team's unconvincing performance in the 0-0 draw with Penang in Saturday's Super League match at the Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Stadium in Kuala Terengganu.
The result saw the home side drop crucial points in their third Super League match of the season.
Nafuzi said the players struggled to settle early in the match, which severely affected their overall play.

5ccda71b3314eccd: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — A worker was killed after falling about seven metres while dismantling scaffolding at a construction site in Bayan Lepas here last Friday.

The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH), in a statement today, said initial investigations found the incident occurred at 1.30 pm, when the victim was descending the scaffolding to take a lunch break.
“While descending the scaffolding, the victim fell from a height of about seven metres onto the floor.
“As a result of the incident, the victim sustained serious head injuries and was taken to Penang Hospital (HPP) for treatment but was pronounced dead,” it said.
Following the incident, Penang DOSH issued a stop work order and a prohibition of interference order to preserve the scene and ensure that investigations could be carried out smoothly.

DOSH said further investigations were underway, including recording statements from the employer and witnesses, to identify the cause of the accident and determine the level of compliance with occupational safety and health legislation.

The investigation is being conducted under Sections 15, 18A and 18B of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994 (Act 514), as well as the relevant occupational safety and health regulations. — Bernama
032436a82b014498: KUALA LUMPUR: A lifelong dream of setting foot on Mount Everest prompted Mohd Sani Harul to join an expedition to Everest Base Camp (EBC) in Nepal before he was reported missing in floods in Rasuwa on Aug 26.

His wife, Nor Azila Shaharuddin, said her husband's passion for mountaineering had led the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia deputy director (Operations) to fulfil his dream by travelling to EBC in a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
"My husband has been interested in mountaineering since he was young, but only within Malaysia. He had climbed Mount Kinabalu three times, as well as Mount Tahan and Mount Ledang.
"He once said Everest had been his dream since he was young, so he wanted to reach EBC at least once, even if only by four-wheel-drive vehicle," she told Bernama here today.
Nor Azila said Sani, 59, had been active in mountaineering since early in his career and was previously a member of the Fire and Rescue Department's Rescue Climbers.
She said her last communication with her husband was via WhatsApp on Aug 26 about 5am Malaysian time, or 3am Nepal time.
According to her, Sani told her he would be travelling to the Nepal-Tibet border, a journey expected to take about five hours by vehicle, before spending the night in Gerung, China.
She said her husband had not activated international roaming during his stay in Nepal, relying instead on hotel Wi-Fi to keep in touch with the family.

Nor Azila said she and her family continued to hope for good news about Sani and other Malaysians still missing in the tragedy, while hoping the targeted search operation by Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) in Nepal would yield results.
"My family and friends have continuously performed special prayers and recited Yasin, praying for the search efforts to succeed and for all Malaysian victims to be found safe," she said.
She also said Wisma Putra had remained in constant contact with her, providing updates on the situation in Nepal at least once a day throughout the search and rescue operation.
Sani was reported missing after the four-wheel-drive vehicle carrying his group during the EBC expedition was believed to have been swept up by floods while they were in a valley in Rasuwa.

A total of 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable following the disaster on Aug 26, while another 77 who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu for the necessary procedures before returning to Malaysia.
Anadolu Agency reported that the death toll from the disaster had risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, remained missing.
f7917f08e5c8287f: PETALING JAYA: Menteri besar Ismail Lasim and the Negeri Sembilan government have expressed their full loyalty and support for the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

This follows a statement by the Secretariat of the Four Undangs calling for the state administration, particularly the state secretary, to comply with a proclamation purportedly signed by Ismail at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on Aug 3 ordering the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the state ruler.
In a statement today, Ismail said his priority was to fulfil his duties as menteri besar in the interests of the people and the state.
“I take note of the media statement issued by the four undangs yesterday. They are entitled to their views,” he said.
15f184642b5b9bb7: KUANTAN, Sept 6 — One participant died while eight others received treatment at hospital after experiencing health problems while taking part in the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) 2026 at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) in Jengka, Maran.
Maran Police chief Supt Wong Kim Wai said police received a report on the incident at 6.59 pm yesterday.
“The deceased was a 21-year-old male student. Further details will be provided after the post-mortem report is received,” he told Bernama when contacted.
It is understood that all of them lost consciousness before being rushed to hospital, with their condition believed to have been due to the hot weather.

Meanwhile, UiTM Pahang branch, in a statement, expressed its profound sadness and extended its condolences to the family of the participant from UiTM Negeri Sembilan branch, the late Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal.
“The university management always prioritises the wellbeing of its members and is therefore giving its full attention to the welfare of the deceased’s family.

“The management has mobilised comprehensive assistance to ensure that all matters relating to the funeral arrangements, documentation, transportation and emotional support for the family are handled smoothly and with ease,” the statement said.
UiTM said that, as part of its commitment to the safety and health of its students, the organisers had cancelled the outdoor events for KKEC 2026 scheduled for today.

According to the statement, the annual programme, which brings together kesatria commanders from all UiTM branches nationwide, is being held from Sept 2 to 8 at UiTM Pahang branch, Jengka Campus, and has been conducted in accordance with strict health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs).

“All participants are required to undergo health screenings before the programme begins, as well as periodic health checks before each event. In fact, several participants had previously been asked to withdraw after failing the final screening,” it said.
The university said it takes the incident very seriously and will continue to closely monitor the situation to ensure the wellbeing of all those involved.
“We deeply regret any inconvenience caused, and greatly appreciate the cooperation and prayers of all parties as we navigate this difficult time,” it said. — Bernama

6a65fd672c6b5f78: PETALING JAYA: A Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student has died, while eight others were hospitalised after suffering heat-related symptoms while taking part in an endurance challenge at the UiTM Jengka campus in Maran, Pahang, on Thursday.

bdcdc3df899a0a85: SINGAPORE, Sept 6 — Singapore has completed its Woodlands North station for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link, four months before the cross-border railway is due to open in January 2027.
The Land Transport Authority (LTA) revealed the completed station in a Facebook post on September 4, as preparations continue for the long-awaited link between northern Singapore and Johor Bahru.
Once operational, the 4km shuttle between Woodlands North and Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru is expected to take about five minutes.

Passengers travelling on the RTS Link will be able to clear both Singapore and Malaysian immigration before boarding, meaning they will not need to undergo immigration clearance again after crossing the border.
Woodlands North station will connect Singapore with Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru via a five-minute RTS journey. — Picture via Facebook/WeKeepYourWorldMoving
Singapore’s immigration facilities are located on basement one of Woodlands North station, while Malaysia’s customs, immigration and quarantine facilities are on basement two.
The station is connected directly to the existing Thomson-East Coast Line, with passengers able to transfer between the two services through a concourse on basement one.
According to LTA’s Facebook post, construction of the station presented significant engineering challenges because of the large amount of hard rock beneath the site.

More than 600 controlled rock-blasting operations were carried out in smaller quantities, timed around train movements on the operational Thomson-East Coast Line. High-capacity drilling machines were also used during the works.
Inside the completed Woodlands North station, where passengers will clear Singapore and Malaysian immigration before boarding RTS trains. — Picture via Facebook/WeKeepYourWorldMoving
LTA said the station’s design draws on Woodlands’ natural surroundings, with colours and architectural elements inspired by trees.
The cross-border viaduct also includes a design feature at the international boundary depicting clasped hands, intended to symbolise the close relationship between Singapore and Malaysia.
The RTS trains will have a maximum speed of 80km/h and the system is designed to carry up to 10,000 passengers an hour in each direction.
The project is expected to significantly increase public transport capacity between Singapore and Johor Bahru and ease pressure on the heavily used road crossings between the two cities.
71f322250ea7e41a: MONZA: Lewis Hamilton was left disappointed on Saturday as the pace in his Ferrari evaporated as he qualified fifth for the Italian Grand Prix behind team-mate Charles Leclerc, the duo later rising to third and fourth following penalties.
Meanwhile championship leader Kimi Antonelli, relegated to the back of the grid following an engine change said he just hoped to pick up some points.

Hamilton, the seven-time champion, was bidding for an outright record sixth pole at Monza where he shares the record of five with Ferrari great Michael Schumacher, said he felt the Mercedes-powered cars ahead remained faster.

"I think we have a really great car," he said. "It's all Mercedes engines up ahead of us and I think we've done a good job to be as close to them as we are, but they ultimately gain several tenths on the straight.
"It is what it is. We just have to do the best we can. We're hoping for tracks that don't rely too much on power hopefully in the future.
"I'm really grateful to the guys back in the factory because they did bring an upgrade here. They are really pushing, but this is just the situation we're in."
Hamilton again struck a note of criticism of the team strategy, saying it left him with no rhythm in his driving.
"The execution in Q3 was pretty bad. I ended up out in the middle of nowhere with nobody," he said, referring to the need for a tow in slipstreaming on the high-speed Monza circuit.
"When you're following another car, you arrive several kilometres faster into a corner so the braking distances adjust.
"It's all about getting into rhythm and I got really out of rhythm for Q3 run one and then Q3 run two. It wasn't a terrible lap, but as I said, the references were all different."
Antonelli, doomed to the back row, said he tried to help title rival and team-mate George Russell.
"It's what I have to do," he said after qualifying seventh. "The team asked me and, of course, I did what I had to do. I tried to help as much as possible.
"It's a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall, with the penalty, I had to be a good team-mate and I had to help as much as I could.
"I think I did a good job with that and I'm happy it worked out."
He added that he expected a tough battle in Sunday's race, but hoped to score points if possible.
"We're going to try to stay out of trouble in the first two chicanes and then obviously try to clear the traffic as quickly as possible in the first few laps and then try to chase the faster cars.
"It will be difficult, but I am going to try to enjoy it." - AFP
23d8224cae6966ed: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) MAS01, which was deployed on a Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission to Nepal, safely arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu at noon local time yesterday.

In a statement today, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) said the team completed its arrival procedures and mission protocols by 4.30 pm local time, including logistics clearance and member manifest verification.
“As of the latest update, the team is en route to the Malaysian Embassy to receive a briefing on the current situation.
“Further coordination will be carried out with the Embassy and local emergency management agencies to determine the team’s deployment arrangements,” Nadma said.
The agency added that Nadma and the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal will coordinate daily mission reports for the duration of the operation.
Nadma also confirmed that all team members are in good health, with no issues reported as of the latest update.
Malaysia’s SMART MAS01 team in Kathmandu receive a briefing in Kathmandu to assist Nepal with humanitarian aid for the flood disaster on September 6, 2026. — Picture from Facebook/Bernama
The media previously reported that 11 SMART personnel departed for Nepal yesterday at 9 am aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft from the Subang Air Base.

Also onboard were 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including rescue gear, detection devices, communication systems, high-capacity drone technology, and specialised tunnel rescue tools, along with a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne cargo truck. — Bernama
9d94c4a4915798bd: SEPTEMBER 6 — The movement of the USS George Washington from Japan toward the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln deserves Asean’s attention for reasons extending beyond naval strategy.
Its redeployment potentially creates a temporary gap in American carrier presence in the Western Pacific. Such gaps are not unprecedented and should not be exaggerated.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

In this US Navy handout photo, an F/A-18 Super Hornet assigned to Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 195, readies for takeoff on the flight deck of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN 73) on August 29, 2026. Iran launched a wave of attacks on US sites across the Middle East on September 2 as violence surged after an extensive American bombardment and the deaths of four people at an Iranian wedding party. — US Navy pic via AFP
Yet the episode demonstrates a fundamental reality of international politics: even the world’s foremost military power cannot deploy unlimited resources everywhere simultaneously.
When the Middle East demands greater American attention, resources available elsewhere can be affected.
For Southeast Asia, the lesson is straightforward. External powers have global priorities. Asean’s priority is Southeast Asia.

This is why the region must think about security more comprehensively. Geopolitics remains important. Geo-economics has become equally important. But there is now a third dimension Asean can no longer regard as merely technological: artificial intelligence sovereignty.
The strategic competition of the twenty-first century will not be determined by aircraft carriers, missiles and military bases alone.
Power increasingly resides in semiconductors, data centres, cloud infrastructure, undersea cables, electricity grids, critical minerals, algorithms and access to advanced computing.

Indeed, Asean’s own Digital Masterplan 2030 recognises that countries and companies able to develop, govern and deploy AI effectively will acquire important advantages in innovation, productivity and influence.
The strategic map of Asia is therefore changing.
Traditional geopolitics asks where military forces are positioned and who controls important maritime passages.

AI geopolitics asks where advanced chips are produced, who controls cloud infrastructure, where data are stored and who possesses the computing and electricity required to operate increasingly powerful AI systems.
Asean cannot remain merely a spectator to this transformation.
Nor should Southeast Asia become simply a market of hundreds of millions of consumers purchasing AI technologies developed and controlled elsewhere.
This is where AI sovereignty becomes important.
AI sovereignty does not mean technological autarky. Indonesia does not need to reproduce the entire American or Chinese technology ecosystem.
Neither does Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand or the Philippines.
It means retaining sufficient control over critical data, infrastructure, talent, regulations and computing capabilities to preserve national and regional agency.
Asean has always prospered through openness.
Japanese investment, American technology, European markets, South Korean manufacturing and Chinese supply chains have all contributed to Southeast Asia’s transformation.
The same principle should guide Asean into the AI age: grow with all, but become dependent on none.
Indonesia has an especially important role.
As Asean’s largest economy and most populous member, Indonesia possesses the domestic scale to influence Southeast Asia’s digital trajectory. But Indonesia does not need to do everything itself.
Asean countries possess complementary capabilities.
Singapore has advanced financial, research and digital infrastructure. Malaysia has an established semiconductor ecosystem and a rapidly expanding data-centre industry.

Vietnam possesses electronics manufacturing capabilities and a growing technology workforce. Thailand brings substantial industrial depth, while the Philippines has a large English-speaking workforce and extensive experience in business-process services.
Asean should connect these capabilities rather than allow them to develop as separate national islands.
This requires a regional approach to AI sovereignty.

Asean does not need one industrial policy for 11 highly diverse member states. It needs interoperability, trusted cross-border data arrangements, cybersecurity cooperation, AI education and research, sufficient computing capacity and the ability to move technology and talent across regional ecosystems.
Universities must be part of this architecture.
So must SMEs.
The greatest economic impact of AI may not ultimately be determined by which Asean country develops the most sophisticated frontier model.
It will depend on whether millions of Southeast Asian businesses can use AI to improve productivity.

Imagine Indonesian, Malaysian, Vietnamese, Thai and Filipino SMEs routinely using AI to manage inventories, improve logistics, translate languages, conduct research, detect fraud and reach international customers.
That would turn AI from an elite technological project into an Asean productivity revolution.
But AI sovereignty has another dimension that Asean cannot ignore: energy.

AI requires enormous quantities of electricity. The Asean Centre for Energy has already warned that AI-driven data-centre expansion could place significant pressure on national electricity systems and local grids.

This makes the Asean Power Grid increasingly relevant to the region’s digital future. Asean has moved from discussing regional electricity integration toward the practical requirements for multilateral power trading.
The relationship is increasingly clear.

Energy security supports digital sovereignty. Digital sovereignty supports AI sovereignty. AI sovereignty strengthens economic resilience. And economic resilience gives Asean greater geopolitical autonomy.
This is why the region should stop treating foreign policy, defence, economics, technology and energy as separate strategic silos.
A semiconductor can simultaneously be a commercial product, technological asset and geopolitical instrument.
A data centre can be private infrastructure, a massive electricity consumer and part of national strategic architecture.
An AI model can improve productivity while simultaneously creating new dependencies.
Asean therefore needs a broader conception of security.

The movement of an American aircraft carrier illustrates the point. The United States will remain an important Indo-Pacific power. China will remain Asean’s largest geographical neighbour and one of its most important economic partners.
Asean should not define its technological future by choosing between them.
Instead, Southeast Asia should cooperate with American, Chinese, Japanese, South Korean, European, Indian and Gulf partners.
Diversification has always been one of Asean’s strongest forms of strategic insurance.

But beneath these partnerships must exist an irreducible layer of Asean capability: scientists, engineers, universities, computing infrastructure, cybersecurity expertise, regulatory competence and businesses capable of developing their own applications.
Otherwise Asean risks entering the AI age economically connected to everyone while technologically dependent on everyone.
Aircraft carriers can move. Capital can move. Supply chains can move. Export controls can change. Technology restrictions can tighten.
Asean cannot control these decisions.
What Southeast Asia can control is the resilience it builds within the region.
Geopolitics matters. Geo-economics matters.
But Indonesia and its Asean partners must now recognise AI sovereignty as an equally important pillar of strategic autonomy.
In the twenty-first century, sovereignty will not be protected by ships and soldiers alone.
It will also depend on who possesses the knowledge, energy, infrastructure and computing power to shape the future.
* Phar Kim Beng, PhD is the Professor of Asean Studies at International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS).

f5f8a57e63ea6dc1: JOHANNESBURG: South Africa produced a brilliant second-half display to earn a 29-24 Test victory over New Zealand in Johannesburg on Saturday, and a 2-1 lead in the four-match series.
Deadlocked 12-12 at half-time, the Springboks powered to a 12-point advantage in the second half before conceding a try after the full-time hooter.
Wing Kurt-Lee Arendse, centre Jesse Kriel and hooker Malcolm Marx scored tries for the Springboks, who were also awarded a penalty try.
Fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicked two conversions from three attempts and also a penalty.
Captain and No.8 Ardie Savea scored two tries for the All Blacks and wing Will Jordan and substitute hooker Samisoni Taukei'aho one each.
Fly-half Ruben Love and full-back Damian McKenzie slotted one conversion each.
Flanker Siya Kolisi became the most successful Springboks captain with 55 Test victories, overtaking 2007 Rugby World Cup-winning hooker John Smit.
"The All Blacks came hard at us in the first 25 minutes, their lungs were pumping. We did well not to concede more points," said Kolisi.
"Then, we fought back. The way we finished was a lot better than we did in the previous two Tests."
New Zealand loose forward Luke Jacobson said: "We started really well, had momentum, but the Springboks played their game in the second half. They got on top."
South Africa suffered a double blow 10 minutes into the first half when full-back Cheslin Kolbe went off injured and Feinberg-Mngomzezulu was yellow-carded.
Kolbe, who converted all 11 goal kicks he took in the first two Tests, suffered a head injury and Feinberg-Mngomezulu was punished for a deliberate knock down of a Savea pass.
New Zealand immediately took advantage of having an extra man to take a seven-point lead through the first of two first-half tries from Savea.
Hooker Asafo Aumua, promoted to the starting line-up in place of the long-serving Codie Taylor, broke from a line-out and when he was halted, Savea picked up the loose ball and dived over.
Power against pace
The return of Feinberg-Mngomezulu coincided with Springbok pressure which culminated in Arendse taking a pass from centre Damian de Allende and scoring in the corner.
Feinberg-Mngomezulu missed the conversion, leaving the hosts trailing 7-5 midway through the first half at Soccer City stadium.
Savea struck again on 26 minutes. After Arendse held up wing Leroy Carter just short of the tryline, the skipper snatched the ball and crossed the whitewash.
A frenetic first half, with the power of the Springboks ranged against the pace of the All Blacks, then took another dramatic turn.
When South Africa won a scrum close to the New Zealand tryline and the visitors backpedalled, referee Nika Amashukeli spotted an infringement and awarded a penalty try.
Adding to the tourists' disappointment, Love was yellow carded.
Ahead of the third Test there had been a war of words with both camps questioning the legality of their rivals' scrummaging tactics.
Georgian Amashukeli policed the set piece well, giving clear instructions to the front rows. No scrum had to be reset until 10 minutes into the second half.
As a tense struggle moved towards the hour mark, Jordan, then Kriel scored tries. Carter had a role in both.
After being tackled, Carter did well to pass to Jordan, but his poor attempt to halt Kriel proved costly. Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted and South Africa led 19-17.
Marx then barged over for a try. Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted and kicked a penalty for a 12-point lead that South Africa retained until a pushover try from Taukei'aho.
The series ends in Baltimore, in the United States, on September 12.

54a64a133c31375e: PETALING JAYA: AirAsia membatalkan atau menjadualkan semula beberapa penerbangan ke dan dari Jakarta susulan letusan gunung berapi Anak Krakatau di Selat Sunda yang menyebabkan Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta di Indonesia ditutup sementara.

Syarikat penerbangan tambang rendah itu berkata, abu gunung berapi menimbulkan ancaman besar kepada keselamatan pesawat, mendorong pelarasan operasi kepada perkhidmatan terpilih yang laluan penerbangannya mungkin terjejas.

"AirAsia telah memaklumkan semua penumpang terjejas mengenai status penerbangan dan pilihan disediakan untuk mereka, AirAsia juga sedang berusaha memastikan penumpang dapat menyambung perjalanan mereka dengan selamat menerusi penerbangan seterusnya yang tersedia," katanya menurut Bernama.
AirAsia menggesa penumpang yang pergi dan balik dari destinasi terjejas menyemak status penerbangan terkini mereka sebelum melakukan perjalanan.
"AirAsia terus memantau aktiviti gunung berapi Anak Krakatau dan akan mengemas kini nasihat perjalanan dengan penyambungan semula operasi seperti biasa."

Sementara itu, Kementerian Pengangkutan Indonesia memaklumkan 209 penerbangan terjejas akibat penutupan sementara Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta disebabkan abu gunung berapi Anak Krakatau.

ed478f1eaa881e21: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Two areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 10am today, with Kuching recording the highest reading nationwide at 223, followed by Sri Aman at 215.
The Air Pollutant Index Management System (Apims) portal reported unhealthy API readings for 35 areas in eight states and three Federal Territories.
Sarawak recorded the highest number with 10 areas, followed by Selangor with six, Johor with four, Negeri Sembilan and Sabah with three each, and Pahang and Melaka with two each.
Kuala Lumpur also recorded two areas with unhealthy API readings, while Terengganu, Putrajaya and Labuan each recorded one.
In Sarawak, unhealthy air quality was recorded in Samalaju at 200, Bintulu at 198, Mukah at 194, Samarahan at 192, Sarikei at 188, IPD Serian and ILP Miri at 182 each, Sibu at 181 and Miri at 175.
In Selangor, the areas with unhealthy API readings were Johan Setia at 180, Shah Alam at 168, Banting and Petaling Jaya at 157 each, and Klang and Kuala Selangor at 154 each.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 163 while Batu Muda recorded 161, while Putrajaya recorded 163.
In Pahang, Jerantut recorded an API reading of 168 while Temerloh recorded 164.
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 167, Seremban 166 and Port Dickson 152.
In Johor, the areas with unhealthy API readings were Segamat at 160, Tangkak at 152, Kluang at 148 and Batu Pahat at 133.
In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 164, Kota Kinabalu 161 and Kimanis 154, while Labuan recorded 161.
In Melaka, Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai each recorded an API reading of 156.
In Terengganu, Paka recorded an unhealthy API reading of 107.
Other areas recorded good to moderate API readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous.
f9060cee27717db5: PARIS: Lens's difficult start to the new season continued on Saturday as Mamadou Kone scored his first Ligue 1 goal to give Lorient a 1-0 win at last season's runners-up.

After Lens sold several key players and lost their coach in the close season, new boss Dino Toppmoeller started brightly by beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions' Trophy and then opening the Ligue 1 campaign with a 5-2 win over Auxerre.
But that was followed by a defeat at Strasbourg and now this second consecutive reverse.
Kone pounced on a loose ball on 54 minutes to score the only goal of the game.
Ahead of their trip to Slavia Prague for a Champions League game on Thursday, Lens showed little fight against an abrasive Lorient.
Monaco top Ligue 1 after snatching a 2-1 win at PSG on Friday, leaving the champions winless so far.
Lens led Ligue 1 for much of last season before finishing just six points behind PSG and winning the French Cup.

In the late games, Ivory Coast forward Elye Wahi snatched a point for Nice in a 1-1 draw at home to Le Mans, while Mali midfielder Kamory Doumbia notched a brace as Brest won 2-1 at 10-man Le Havre, who had Junior Mwanga dismissed. - AFP
f9acc1f0c920e08a: NEW YORK, Sept 6 — Two-time US Open champion Naomi Osaka survived another erratic outing, beating Belgian Elise Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5 yesterday to reach the US Open fourth round.
Osaka had 41 unforced errors, her backhand in particular letting her down as she was unable to build on a comfortable first set for the second straight match.
“I’m literally shocked that I won this match,” Osaka, seeded 13th, told an adoring crowd in Louis Armstrong Stadium.
“There was a certain point where I felt like I put my entire heart on the court. I just kept trying every point.”
After an early exchange of breaks in the second set, Osaka failed to convert a pair of chances and Mertens broke again for a 5-3 lead.
Osaka gifted the Belgian two break points with a double fault, saving one with a forehand winner before sailing a backhand wide.
Mertens finally took the set when Osaka dumped a backhand into the net.
Mertens kept the pressure on in the third and was rewarded with a break for a 3-2 lead, aided by a string of backhand errors from Osaka.
Osaka was clearly frustrated, berating herself and exchanging some testy words with her team.
“I didn’t feel like I played amazing, it was really getting me down,” she told the crowd, offering an apology for her behaviour.
She was down a break trailing 4-3 when she took a medical timeout for treatment on her left calf and ankle.
Osaka returned with renewed vigour, breaking Mertens at love for 4-4 and saving a break point in the next game for a 5-4 lead.
Mertens didn’t go quietly, saving a match point on the way to 5-5 and saving two more in the final game before Osaka secured the win. — AFP
186ad2e2cfbf7ccc: KUALA LUMPUR: The telecommunications industry's core earnings per share (EPS) are expected to improve quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The firm said the improvement would be supported by positive seasonality, better mobile monetisation and robust demand for fibre connectivity.
Meanwhile, CIMB Securities said the review of the Mandatory Standard on Access Pricing (MSAP) may begin between September and October and be finalised by December 2026 or January 2027.
It added that the Finance Ministry's transfer of its shares in Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) to Maxis Bhd, CelcomDigi Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd could be completed by the end of Q3 2026.
"Thereafter, the market should gain more clarity on DNB's net loss and the telcos' plans to reduce the impact on their profit and loss over the next two to three years," it said.
CIMB Securities said most telcos under its coverage reported Q2 2026 core EPS in line with its and consensus forecasts.
The exception was Axiata Group Bhd, whose first-half 2026 core EPS surged 260 per cent year-on-year (YoY), outperforming expectations on the back of strong contributions from XLS, Robi and Dialog.

Time dotCom Bhd and Maxis also delivered a strong quarter, in line with expectations, supported by healthy revenue growth at Time and stronger earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margins at both companies.
Following the Q2 2026 results, CIMB Securities said it made no changes to its stock ratings.
However, it raised its target prices for Time and Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) by two per cent and nine per cent, respectively, while cutting Axiata's target price by 10 per cent.
The firm also lowered its financial year 2026 to 2028 (FY26 to FY28) dividend per share (DPS) forecasts for Time to 42 to 43 sen.
CIMB Securities noted that industry mobile service revenue inched up 0.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) and 0.1 per cent QoQ in Q2 2026.
Postpaid revenue continued to grow steadily, rising 1.8 per cent YoY, while prepaid revenue remained soft, declining 1.9 per cent YoY.
However, the decline was an improvement from the three to seven per cent YoY contraction recorded between Q3 2024 and Q3 2025.
"We foresee the prepaid revenue trend gradually improving in the second half of 2026, as the competitive landscape has become more constructive in the first half," it said.
Maxis' mobile revenue market share (RMS) increased by 0.2 percentage point QoQ to 43.6 per cent in Q2 2026, while CelcomDigi's RMS fell to 56.4 per cent.

In Q2 2026, industry fixed services revenue grew 7.2 per cent YoY, led by TM, which recorded seven per cent growth, Time, which also grew seven per cent, and CelcomDigi's fixed business, which rose 36 per cent YoY.
Fixed broadband (FBB) subscriptions grew modestly by 0.7 per cent QoQ and 3.6 per cent YoY, in line with a maturing market.
CelcomDigi's net additions of 22,000 remained strong, exceeding the combined net additions of TM, Maxis and Time, which totalled 13,000.
FBB average revenue per user remained largely stable YoY, reflecting stabilising price competition.

08c9316d00af907f: PETALING JAYA: Kedutaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) di Kuala Lumpur menafikan dakwaan bahawa ia pernah cuba untuk menentukan kepimpinan politik Malaysia dan menyifatkannya sebagai dakwaan palsu.
Kuasa Usaha Sementara Kedutaan AS, David H Gamble Jr, berkata AS tidak pernah berusaha untuk menentukan siapa yang memimpin Malaysia.
“AS tidak pernah berusaha untuk menentukan siapa yang menjadi pemimpin politik Malaysia.
"Sebarang dakwaan yang mengatakan sebaliknya adalah palsu,” katanya dalam kenyataan di Facebook hari ini.
Beliau membuat penafian itu susulan dakwaan campur tangan AS dalam politik di Malaysia.
Terdahulu, Presiden PAS Hadi Awang dilaporkan mendakwa parti itu pernah ditawarkan pihak asing untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan.

Beliau membuat dakwaan berkenaan ketika menyampaikan ucapan penggulungan pada Muktamar Tahunan PAS Ke-72 di Kota Bharu, semalam.

Takiyuddin yang ditemui pemberita selepas muktamar mengesahkan perkara itu tetapi menjelaskan perbincangan tidak lebih daripada persoalan sama ada PAS mempunyai rancangan untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan Barisan Nasional (BN), yang tidak dijawab oleh PAS.
Kedutaan AS sebelum ini turut menegaskan bahawa hubungan diplomatiknya dengan Malaysia terus memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh hubungan dua hala antara kedua-dua negara.
6dfaf450740060f9: PETALING JAYA: The US embassy has denied that it offered to help topple the government in 2014, following a claim by PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang.
Charge d’Affaires David H Gamble Jr said the US has never sought to decide Malaysia's political leadership.
“Any account to the contrary is false,” he said in a statement.
At PAS’s muktamar yesterday, Hadi claimed that the party was offered assistance by the US to topple the government in 2014.
He said this took place at a meeting at the embassy during the visit of former US president Barack Obama, attended by several PAS leaders.
He said then PAS assistant secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan and Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who was Hadi’s political secretary at the time, went to the embassy for the meeting.
However, Takiyuddin and Samsuri were not swayed by the offer and remained firm in rejecting it, he said.
Hadi also claimed that after the meeting, the US ambassador requested a separate meeting with him, which he attended with Mustafa Ali, then PAS secretary-general.
He said the ambassador asked him for the name of PAS’s proposed prime minister, to which he responded by saying, “Who does America agree with?”
Hadi said he recounted the incident to former prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who said it was “good”.

Barisan Nasional was ousted from Putrajaya in the 2018 general election, with the then opposition Pakatan Harapan’s campaign focused heavily on the 1MDB scandal and corruption allegations against then prime minister Najib Razak.
PH won the elections and Mahathir was subsequently sworn in as the prime minister.
81270e61dd1bc74a: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission (SC) and Bursa Malaysia Bhd have launched the inaugural InvestSmart x Bursa Marketplace Fair 2026 to strengthen investor education and protection against investment scams.
The two-day event brought together the SC and Bursa Malaysia's flagship investor engagement platforms for the first time.
It was officiated by Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.

The collaboration aimed to highlight the importance of investor education and financial literacy in supporting informed and responsible investing, as more Malaysians navigate a wider range of investment products, digital platforms and information sources.
The SC said the collaboration reflects a shared commitment with Bursa Malaysia to advance investor education effectively.

By bringing together the two-flagship investor engagement platforms, both organisations aim to broaden their outreach, delivering greater impact in promoting informed investing and investor protection.

The event combined investor education, market insights and practical guidance to better equip participants with the knowledge to evaluate investment opportunities, understand risks and identify potential scams.
SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said broader participation in the capital market remains essential to support a financially resilient and inclusive society.
"For many Malaysians, concerns over fraud and limited access to reliable investment information remain barriers to investing.

"This first-ever collaboration aims to improve access to trusted financial information and digital investment tools, empowering more Malaysians to invest with confidence and take greater charge of their long-term financial well-being," he said in a statement.

Faiz said the SC remains committed to strengthening investor education and financial literacy through strategic partnerships, including with the National Scam Response Centre and the Financial Education Network.

From January to July 2026, the SC received 1,272 enquiries (70.6 per cent) from individuals seeking to verify investment opportunities before making any investments, compared with 530 complaints (29.4 per cent) from scam victims.
The higher proportion of enquiries points to greater awareness of the need to conduct due diligence before investing.

Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk said the local capital market offers a wide range of opportunities for investors, and the growing participation of Malaysians, particularly younger investors.
This reflects a growing interest among Malaysians in building financial resilience.

"By bringing market experts, listed companies and financial institutions under one roof, we hope to make it easier for more Malaysians to explore investment opportunities, build their knowledge and take the next step from saving to investing.
"This supports our broader goal of fostering a vibrant and inclusive capital market that enables more Malaysians to participate in, and benefit from, the nation's economic growth," he noted.

Retail participation in the capital market continues to strengthen, with more than 342,000 new Central Depository System (CDS) accounts opened in the first six months of 2026, up about 24 per cent from the corresponding period last year.
Around 60 per cent of the new accounts were opened by investors aged 35 and below, reflecting growing participation among younger Malaysians.
Retail investors also accounted for between 27 per cent and 33 per cent of total trading activity over the past three years.

The fair brought together up to 40 exhibitors, giving visitors direct access to market experts, financial intermediaries, regulators, public-listed companies, crowdfunding platforms and other industry practitioners.

ae88ed33c75483b0: COPENHAGEN: EU chief Ursula von der Leyen heads to Greenland on Sunday for a two-day visit aimed at reaffirming the bloc's support for the Danish autonomous territory coveted by US President Donald Trump.
On Monday, she is due to sign a joint declaration between the EU and Greenland.

"Greenland is becoming increasingly important to the EU as a gateway to the Arctic and because of its geopolitical location, critical raw materials and role in Arctic security," Marc Jacobsen, a researcher at the Royal Danish Defence College, told AFP.
Trump was adamant earlier this year about Washington's need to control the vast Arctic island for reasons of national security, though he ultimately ruled out annexing it by force.
A Danish-Greenlandic-US working group has since met regularly to find an agreement on cooperation going forward.
Following Trump's threats, European countries broadly backed Denmark and Greenland, and in January von der Leyen vowed "massive" EU investment in Greenland to step up security in the Arctic.
Greenland is not a member of the bloc though Denmark is.
Brussels has also proposed doubling direct EU aid to Greenland to €530 million under the bloc's next budget for the 2028–2034 period.
According to the Financial Times, von der Leyen is expected to propose an additional €200 million in support during her visit on Sunday and Monday.
Her visit coincides with the start of Nato's Arctic Shield military exercise, bringing together soldiers from 10 countries.
Mikaa Blugeon-Mered, a geopolitics researcher at the University of Quebec, called the timing a "not insignificant coincidence".
The Trump administration has repeatedly accused Denmark of neglecting Greenland and Arctic security.
Copenhagen has since reinvested in the region, as has Nato, which launched its Arctic Sentry mission at the start of the year.

"The EU cannot provide Greenland with a military security guarantee in the way Nato can, but it can provide something politically important: a clear signal that Greenland is not standing alone," Jacobsen said.
Pressure
The message is all the more important as the US has kept up pressure on Greenland -- though Trump has been less vocal since a May visit by his special envoy Jeff Landry.
"We've been getting 'postcards' from Trump or those close to him about Greenland every month, showing that they haven't forgotten," noted Blugeon-Mered.
One such image Trump posted on Truth Social in May showed him peering over the island, with the headline "Hello, Greenland!".
In August, media reports of an American oil company's preparatory operations in a remote region of eastern Greenland rekindled concerns on the island.
The project, run by a Texas-based company with licenses granted before a 2021 moratorium on oil and gas exploration and extraction, has left locals and authorities uneasy.
Authorities have yet to grant the company approval for exploratory drilling, citing procedural reasons.
Greenland is also struggling to develop its mining industry, which could help it fund its independence from Denmark.
In this area, Greenlandic and European interests are "highly complementary", Jacobsen said.
"Greenland needs investment, infrastructure and markets if it is to realise its mining ambitions, while the EU is looking for more secure and diversified access to critical raw materials," he said.
But turning Greenland's geological potential into reality is proving more difficult than expected.
Some 135 mining permits are held by more than 60 companies, but only two mines are currently in operation.
"The question is whether the current geopolitical momentum will ultimately be a game-changer," Jacobsen said.
Blugeon-Mered said von der Leyen's visit to Greenland -- her second in two years -- was a strong signal that European investment is long-term.

The EU chief is scheduled to hold talks during her visit with Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and the head of government of Denmark's other self-governing territory, the Faroe Islands.
d64b79f5d70f4cdb: GENEVA, Sept 6 — Nearly 130 countries yesterday agreed on a text defining lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS) — “killer robots” to their critics — a first step towards talks on a possible international treaty to regulate them.
The text agreed upon has not yet been made public — but campaign groups following the talks have already criticised leading countries for dragging their feet on the issue.
Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen announced the agreement, by 128 countries, yesterday. The Netherlands has been overseeing the talks.
Countries are already developing and using weapons capable of selecting targets and using force against them without human intervention.

But the International Committee of the Red Cross warned in a statement that “the unconstrained development and use of autonomous weapon systems pose serious legal, ethical and humanitarian challenges”.
The ICRC and several campaigning groups have called for international legally binding rules to restrict and regulate their use.
Nicole van Rooijen, executive director of Stop Killer Robots, an international alliance of campaign groups, accused the United States, Russia and their allies of trying to weaken the agreed text.
Lex International, a Geneva-based philanthropic group funding work on key policy issues, also criticised some nations’ position.
“The United States, Russia, India and Israel are amongst the key opponents of negotiations,” it said.
“The governments of Brazil, Ireland, and Norway are leading efforts to get such negotiations started in November,” it added.
UN member states will decide at November talks of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons whether to move towards an international treaty regulating such weapons. — AFP
a756a81f6254f543: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pelajar Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) meninggal dunia akibat masalah berkaitan haba ketika menyertai Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) di kampus UiTM Jengka, Maran, Jumaat lalu.
Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, meninggal dunia di Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah (HoSHAS), Temerloh, tengah hari semalam.
Ketua Polis Maran, Wong Kim Wai, mengesahkan mangsa itu antara dua pelajar yang dirawat di HoSHAS, manakala tujuh lagi dirawat di Hospital Jengka.
Menurutnya, hasil pemeriksaan awal mendapati pelajar itu mengalami masalah berkaitan haba, termasuk kekurangan oksigen ketika menyertai acara terbabit.
"Perkembangan lanjut akan diberikan selepas menerima laporan bedah siasat Fadhlan Fakhry," katanya menurut Berita Harian.
Sementara itu, UiTM Pahang dalam kenyataan mengumumkan semua aktiviti luar KKEC yang dijadualkan hari ini dibatalkan dan menzahirkan ucapan takziah kepada keluarga Fadhlan Fakhry.

"Universiti menggerakkan bantuan menyeluruh bagi memastikan segala urusan berkaitan jenazah, dokumentasi, pengangkutan serta sokongan emosi kepada keluarga diuruskan dengan sebaik mungkin dan tanpa kesulitan."
Katanya, Fadhlan Fakhry ialah pelajar tahun akhir program diploma di kampus Seremban dan mewakili UiTM Negeri Sembilan dalam acara berkenaan.

Jelasnya, KKEC ialah program tahunan membabitkan peserta Komander Kesatria dari cawangan UiTM seluruh negara. Ia adalah pertandingan ketahanan fizikal dan mental tahunan yang direka untuk menguji kekuatan fizikal, kemahiran taktikal, ketangkasan serta kerja berpasukan dalam kalangan pelajar.
Menurutnya, program yang berlangsung dari 2 hingga 8 Sept ini di kampus UiTM Jengka itu mematuhi prosedur operasi standard kesihatan serta keselamatan ketat.

"Semua peserta diwajibkan menjalani saringan kesihatan sebelum program bermula, selain pemeriksaan kesihatan berkala sebelum setiap acara," katanya sambil menambah beberapa peserta diminta menarik diri selepas gagal dalam saringan akhir.
Tegasnya, UiTM mengambil serius kejadian itu dan akan terus memantau keadaan bagi memastikan kebajikan semua pihak terpelihara.
50e03479f640240b: ROME, Sept 6 — A last-gasp winner from Lautaro Martinez sealed a breathless win for Inter as the Serie A champions fought back from two goals down to edge visiting Napoli 3-2, while Roma also pulled off a late turnaround to beat Atalanta 2-1.
Inter and Roma sit joint-top of the table on a perfect nine points, while Atalanta are on six points and Napoli have three.
“It was a beautiful and entertaining match to watch, a great advert for Italian football,” Inter coach Cristian Chivu told DAZN.
“At 2-2 both teams played an open game without thinking of defending the result, I saw big chances at both ends.”
Both goalkeepers were forced into early saves in an end-to-end encounter that remained goalless at half-time after Federico Dimarco’s free-kick rattled the Napoli cross bar.
The game exploded in the second half when Matteo Politano guided home a shot in the 50th minute before Rasmus Hojlund’s curler doubled the Napoli lead three minutes later.

Inter responded almost immediately when Martinez hammered in his first goal of the season from a Dimarco cross. Substitute Marcus Thuram came agonisingly close to a leveller when he headed off the post.
The France international would not be denied twice, though, and smashed a towering header past Alex Meret in the 82nd minute to level the scores.

Chances fell at both ends before Martinez’s penalty box instincts proved decisive in the 91st minute as Napoli failed to clear in a goalmouth scramble and the Argentina striker pounced to settle an extraordinary match.
“I’m happy we managed to fight back, that was missing last year,” Martinez told DAZN.
“Every year we are raising the bar and trying to show that on the pitch.”
Both sides begin their Champions League campaigns next week, when Inter travel to Real Madrid and Napoli host Arsenal on Tuesday.
Dying minutes
In Rome, Mario Hermoso and Matias Soule struck in the dying minutes to continue a perfect start to the season for Roma against their coach Gian Piero Gasperini’s former club Atalanta.

Ederson’s bullet strike early in the second half came against the run of play but looked enough for a backs-to-the-wall victory as Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi kept out wave after wave of Giallorossi attacks.

Roma scored eight goals in their opening two wins of the season, but looked almost out of ideas after replacement striker Santiago Castro was twice denied by the woodwork and Carnesecchi produced a terrific double save.
But Hermoso was left unmarked and looped a header into the far corner to level the scores in the 90th minute.

The Roma players sprinted back to the centre circle as they looked for a quick restart to push for a winner, and that was exactly what they got when substitute Soule fired a composed finish in at the near post to send the Stadio Olimpico wild.

Roma’s first win over Atalanta since March 2022, a run of eight matches, will come as a confidence-booster before their eight-year wait to return to the Champions League ends away to Fenerbahce on Thursday.
Earlier, a late Che Adams strike sealed a 2-1 comeback win for Torino as Fiorentina’s nightmare start to the season continued.

Mateo Pellegrino’s long-range strike put Fiorentina in front early in the second half, but a pile-driver from Rolando Mandragora — who had only joined Torino from La Viola four days earlier — drew the scores level and Scotland international Adams sealed his side’s first points of the season in the 82nd minute with a clever flick.
Fiorentina signed 13 players and appointed new coach Fabio Grosso over the summer after a humbling 15th-place finish last season.
The two-time Italian champions have lost their first three games by an aggregate score of 9-1, and were booed off by their own fans following a performance that left them in last place. — AFP
62780e9a5b11a6b2: NEW YORK: Two-time US Open champion Naomi Osaka survived another erratic outing, beating Belgian Elise Mertens 6-3, 3-6, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the US Open fourth round.
Osaka had 41 unforced errors, her backhand in particular letting her down as she was unable to build on a comfortable first set for the second straight match.
"I'm literally shocked that I won this match," Osaka, seeded 13th, told an adoring crowd in Louis Armstrong Stadium.
"There was a certain point where I felt like I put my entire heart on the court. I just kept trying every point."
After an early exchange of breaks in the second set, Osaka failed to convert a pair of chances and Mertens broke again for a 5-3 lead.
Osaka gifted the Belgian two break points with a double fault, saving one with a forehand winner before sailing a backhand wide.
Mertens finally took the set when Osaka dumped a backhand into the net.
Mertens kept the pressure on in the third and was rewarded with a break for a 3-2 lead, aided by a string of backhand errors from Osaka.
Osaka was clearly frustrated, berating herself and exchanging some testy words with her team.
"I didn't feel like I played amazing, it was really getting me down," she told the crowd, offering an apology for her behavior.
She was down a break trailing 4-3 when she took a medical timeout for treatment on her left calf and ankle.
Osaka returned with renewed vigor, breaking Mertens at love for 4-4 and saving a break point in the next game for a 5-4 lead.
Mertens didn't go quietly, saving a match point on the way to 5-5 and saving two more in the final game before Osaka secured the win.
0da34c51c78f5240: IPOH: Selama 16 tahun berkhidmat di Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM), penolong pegawai perubatan Mariapan Kalaipan menyaksikan sendiri perubahan cara klinik kesihatan menguruskan pesakit – daripada bergantung kepada buku giliran dan timbunan fail fizikal kepada sistem digital yang merekodkan setiap pergerakan pesakit secara masa nyata.

Mariapan yang sedang berkhidmat di Klinik Kesihatan Greentown, berkata peralihan kepada Sistem Pengurusan Digital Berasaskan Awan (CCMS) bukan sekadar menggantikan kaedah manual, malah memudahkan petugas menguruskan aliran pesakit dengan lebih teratur dan telus.
"Dulu selepas pendaftaran, kita susun buku mengikut giliran. Kadang-kadang ada pesakit kata mereka datang lebih awal, tetapi kita tak ada rekod untuk sahkan sebab semuanya dibuat secara manual.
"Sekarang, setiap pesakit masuk dalam sistem giliran. Kita boleh nampak tarikh, masa dia daftar dan bila dia masuk giliran.

"Contohnya dia datang 4.30 petang, sedangkan kita sudah memanggil nombor yang didaftarkan pada 4.20 petang. Kalau pesakit mempertikaikan giliran, kita boleh semak terus dalam sistem. Data itu memudahkan kerja kami," katanya dalam Program Kembara Media ke Perak anjuran Unit Komunikasi Korporat KKM.
Pelaksanaan CCMS di klinik kesihatan antara langkah KKM memperluaskan pendigitalan perkhidmatan kesihatan awam.

Selari usaha memperluaskan pendigitalan sektor kesihatan, jurucakap kerajaan Fahmi Fadzil pada 30 Ogos lalu mengumumkan peruntukan memperkukuh akses digital sektor kesihatan awam dinaikkan daripada RM650 juta kepada RM1 bilion, termasuk bagi pelaksanaan Sistem Rekod Perubatan Elektronik (EMR) dan CCMS.
Inisiatif itu sebahagian daripada enam ikhtiar segera kerajaan sempena Hari Kebangsaan yang mula dilaksanakan 1 Sept lalu.

Klinik Kesihatan Greentown, yang berkhidmat kepada masyarakat setempat selama puluhan tahun, antara fasiliti kesihatan primer utama di bawah Pejabat Kesihatan Daerah Kinta yang melaksanakan CCMS sebagai sebahagian usaha pendigitalan pengurusan klinik.

Menurut Mariapan, perubahan itu bukan sahaja memudahkan urusan di kaunter pendaftaran, malah membantu melancarkan keseluruhan aliran rawatan apabila setiap pesakit dapat dijejaki dengan lebih sistematik dari saat mereka mendaftar sehingga selesai menerima rawatan.
Perubahan itu turut dirasai di bilik pemeriksaan.

Pakar perunding perubatan keluarga, Dr Norliza Muksan, yang berkhidmat selama tiga dekad dengan KKM, berkata pelaksanaan CCMS membantu menangani antara isu sering dibangkitkan pesakit di klinik kesihatan, iaitu tempoh menunggu lama apabila proses mencari fail fizikal dihapuskan.
"Untuk perspektif pesakit, mereka nampak proses lebih cepat, terutama semasa pendaftaran.
"Kita dah potong satu proses, iaitu mencari fail. Bila proses itu dipercepatkan, pesakit boleh menjalani pemeriksaan awal seperti tekanan darah, nadi dan gula.
"Secara tidak langsung, proses lain juga menjadi lebih cepat."
Jelasnya, sistem diintegrasi dengan MySejahtera itu juga memudahkan doktor mengakses rekod rawatan pesakit di fasiliti lain yang menggunakan CCMS dan memastikan kesinambungan rawatan.
"Ada pesakit datang kepada kami tanpa surat. Ada yang tidak tahu nama ubat atau penyakit dihidapi.
"Kalau pesakit mendapatkan rawatan di Pulau Pinang menggunakan CCMS, kemudian datang ke Greentown atau mana-mana klinik yang menggunakan sistem sama, kami masih boleh melihat rekod rawatan mereka.
"Dengan adanya rekod perubatan dalam CCMS, kami boleh membaca rekod pesakit dan memastikan kesinambungan rawatan."
5b146d6ab2bc0fb1: BERLIN, Sept 6 — Defending champions Bayern Munich were held to a scoreless draw by promoted Schalke in the Bundesliga yesterday.
The draw ended Bayern’s run of 67 consecutive matchdays atop the Bundesliga table. It was the first time they failed to score since February 2025.
Seven-time German champions Schalke have not beaten Bayern since 2011 and had not even taken a point off the Bavarian giants in nine years — a run of 12 straight defeats.
“That’s who we are. That’s what defines us, and everyone can be proud of their performance today,” said the impressive Schalke goalie Loris Karius, who was named man of the match.
The former Liverpool ‘keeper deflected the post-match praise to his defenders, telling Sky Germany: “I just had to shout instructions to the lads: keep going, push up, drop back.”
With Harry Kane and Michael Olise starting from the bench, Bayern dominated the ball but created few clear chances as stubborn Schalke dug deep to pick up their first point of the season.
Luis Diaz had an excellent chance with 54 minutes gone when through on the advancing Karius, but the Colombian’s chip was too soft and was cleared off the line by Robin Gosens.
Bayern’s best chance came late when a long-range Kane effort was kept out by an excellent save from Karius, who leapt high to palm the ball to safety.
His opposite number, Bayern captain Manuel Neuer was heavily booed by home fans every time he touched the ball on his return to the club where he started his career.
It will likely be the 40-year-old’s final match in Gelsenkirchen, his home town, before his expected retirement at the season’s end.
“A win would have been nice,” Neuer said, adding “but some of my family will be happy about the result and so it’s okay as it is. I enjoyed myself.”
Despite the defeat, Bayern will be buoyed by the return of Jamal Musiala, who revealed he is suffering from a neurological condition after collapsing in pre-season games.
Nwaneri helps Dortmund on debut
Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri provoked a late own goal as Borussia Dortmund came from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim.
Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.
Nwaneri, the youngest player in Premier League history, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played.
“I liked what I saw,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac said of Nwaneri. “That’s what we brought him in for... Maybe it wasn’t officially his goal, but he created it.”
“The team played all or nothing football,” Kovac added. “And when you (do that)... the gaps start opening up.”
Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle.
Striker Serhou Guirassy gave the visitors hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fabio Silva five minutes later.
In the 86th minute, Nwaneri cut down the left and squared a shot which took a big deflection off home defender Albian Hajdari and landed in the net.
Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.
Elversberg fought back from 3-1 down and took the lead in stoppage time when Maurice Krattenmacher scored the winner.
Elversberg, with a population of just 13,000, are the smallest town ever to have a German top-flight side but opened the season with a shock 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen last week.

Leverkusen rebounded from that disappointment by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory, with Argentina internationals Equi Fernandez and Facundo Medina, Patrik Schick and Ibrahim Maza on target.
Elsewhere, West Ham loanee Niclas Fuellkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen to a surprise 3-1 home win against RB Leipzig.
Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win away at promoted Paderborn. — AFP

cb1bc09923b09b82: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 6 — Malaysia’s fuel supply remains stable despite lower global supply levels, with the government confident it can secure sufficient supplies through to the end of the year, said the prime minister’s economic adviser Nurhisham Hussein.

Nurhisham, who also heads the Secretariat of the National Economic Action Council (MTEN) Crisis Management Task Force, said the global fuel situation has remained fluid. Risks, however, remained skewed towards higher prices due to geopolitical tensions and disruptions to key shipping routes, he added.
Malaysia is a major importer of crude oil but is a net exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

Global oil supplies have been severely affected due to the West Asia conflict, which erupted in February and has shown no signs of ending, with continued attacks between the United States and Iran till today.
Nurhisham reckons that countries are likely to rebuild their oil reserves only when prices returned to more reasonable levels of around US$80 per barrel.

“So, we will have a very slow rebuilding of reserves by these countries, but that implies as well that over the next two to three years oil prices will continue to be elevated. It might not shoot up, but it will continue to be elevated. It’s still a very fluid situation as far as fuels are concerned,” he told a media briefing on the global supply crisis on Friday.

The economic adviser noted that the Suez Canal and Bab-el-Mandeb have remained open despite continuing threats, while damage to Russian facilities and the United States’ blockade of Iranian exports are among factors that could affect global oil supplies. He said the depletion of reserves would eventually remove one source of supply and that would add to uncertainty in the global energy market.

During the one-hour briefing, Nurhisham also shared that China’s rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) was helping to moderate global oil demand and that there had been a significant increase in EV purchases among Chinese consumers. This had helped ameliorate oil demand, he noted.
“At the same time, Chinese refineries were operating at about 80 to 90 per cent capacity originally because of external demand, so they’re actually doing a lot of exports as well,” he said.
Global food outlook

On the global food outlook, Nurhisham said the latest reports indicated a strong El Niño that could persist into February 2027. He noted that Pacific Ocean temperatures in the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) area were already about two degrees above normal.

“That’s already an indicator of a strong El Niño. It has not arrived here yet, and the UN office’s projection is that we’re probably looking at some time in October or November before we really start feeling it. It does feel like we’ve got El Niño already, but that will also have a significant impact around the world. It’s not just Southeast Asia. It’s South Asia, Central and Southern Africa as well, as well as the Caribbean and Latin America,” he added.

Nurhisham said the changing weather patterns are significant for Malaysia given its dependence on imports from some of these regions. Latin America is an important source of food-related feedstock while India is also a major trading partner for food inputs and food products.

Based on the latest Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) projections that he shared during the briefing, global rice supplies are expected to fall 1.6 per cent next year, and this comes against an estimated one per cent increase in demand.

Global stocks could therefore decline by about two per cent, he said, adding that wheat production was also expected to fall by 3.8 per cent, with some regions seeing up to 26 per cent declines, while maize production is projected to drop 2.7 per cent.
“On the flip side, soy is expected to continue to record numbers. So, it’s not all bad. Certain crops are going to do well, certain crops that will not do so well,” he said.

However, he cautioned that seasonal products such as vegetables and eggs could still see changes in supply and prices. For Malaysia, he said the overall food supply situation remained adequate, thanks to the supply which exceeded demand by about 10 per cent across most categories being monitored.
Fuel sufficiency

On Malaysia’s immediate supply position, Nurhisham said fuel sufficiency was guaranteed through the end of September. “Petronas is confident that we’ll be able to (have enough supply) through the end of the year (and) that they’ll be able to get supplies.”

As for “industrial materials and supplies, so far we have not had significant shortages, but certain small and medium enterprises have faced real supply shortages. But so far, whatever we require, we’ve been able to get, including things like plastics,” he revealed. The medical devices and medicines supply situation was also stable.

Nurhisham said fewer than half a dozen medicine categories were considered critical, with most having alternative remedies or medicines available. He cited antihistamines, where several alternatives were available in the market.
On inflation, Nurhisham said the overall situation remained relatively manageable at about two per cent annually and that food inflation was also broadly in line with the prevailing trend.

“Food inflation is roughly still in line with the trend. There are certain pockets where we’re seeing price increases, and there has been some fallout or pass-through from higher energy prices, especially diesel. But obviously, with the recent announcement on the increase in monthly allocation of the Budi Madani RON95, we’re hoping to be able to ameliorate that,” he continued.
The basic monthly eligibility limit under Budi Madani RON 95 has increased from 200 to 300 litres effective Sept 1 this year.

The Ministry of Finance said the adjustment covers Budi Madani RON95 and Budi Madani Diesel, with eligible recipients entitled to up to 300 litres monthly. The subsidised price remains RM1.99 per litre for RON95 and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under the respective schemes.

Nurhisham also said the government might need to accelerate some spending to fund critical infrastructure projects, including water and electricity generation projects, amid growing needs in these areas.
However, he said the government’s longer-term fiscal consolidation objective remains unchanged, with the deficit target still aimed at three per cent of gross domestic product.

“The target may have to be adjusted for the current year due to the need for additional spending, but the government does not expect further changes to the fiscal consolidation path from next year onward. This year, unfortunately, we had to move it. But next year (onward), it should not. There are certain ‘pockets’ where we’re seeing price increases,” he added. — Bernama
e44398e546cfb945: GEORGE TOWN, Sep 6 — Root House by gēn opened this year inside the newly restored 1926 Heritage Hotel on Jalan Burma, the latest restaurant from chef Johnson Wong following gēn and Communal Table by gēn.
The recipient of the Michelin Guide Kuala Lumpur and Penang 2024 Young Chef Award, Wong built his name by spotlighting Penang produce at his fine-dining flagship, gēn.

Root House takes the same produce and explores it through a distinctly Malaysian-Chinese lens, spread across the dialect groups that shape it: Hokkien, Fuzhou, Cantonese, Teochew, Hakka and Hainanese.

Wong is careful about how that premise gets described, though. “We’re not trying to trace old recipes,” he says. “We are researching them, looking at how they changed when they arrived in Malaysia, and why the food we know today is the way it is.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Chef Johnson Wong (right) with the head chef of Root House, Chef Koh Chin Hong (left). Both are natives of Johor. — Picture courtesy of Root House by gēn

The idea took shape after a post-pandemic trip to China. “I was very impressed by the level of cooking — not just in fine dining, but at every level,” he says. “It gave me a lot of ideas to create something of my own like that.”

Even gēn, he admits, still falls into convention. “We’ve focused on local produce throughout the years at gēn, but if you go deep down, Western fundamentals are still at the core. We wanted to do something different, with Chinese soul and technique but with a modern approach.”
Steamed fish, ubiquitous throughout Malaysian-Chinese restaurants, is the example he uses when describing the change between the food he found in China and the food he grew up with.
“We tend to use soy sauce because it’s the easiest way to bring out umami in seafood, but there are many other ways to achieve the same thing that we don’t see here often,” he says.
“One thing I saw there was an old Cantonese technique that uses chicken fat to get that flavour, but cleaner.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Root House is located in the newly restored colonial-style 1926 Heritage Hotel. — Picture courtesy of Root House by gēn

A native of Johor, he traces the difference back to necessity. “Because we arrived in Malaysia as immigrants, a lot of the recipes and cooking techniques were simplified with shortcuts, adding stuff like sugar or cornstarch to make things tastier.
“I can’t say it’s a bad thing, but we just wanted to understand the reason behind it and how we can evolve it heading into the future.”
He points at sugar as an example. “I think when Malaysians eat Chinese food, we tend to have a sweeter palate, having become accustomed to a lot of added sugar.”
At Root House, that sweetness gives way to something purer — the signature threadfin is steamed with curry-infused chicken fat instead of soy.
Less sauce, and more of what he calls the ingredient’s “original flavour”, but with curry as the nod to Malaysia.

“What impressed me the most during my time in China was how light the Cantonese cuisine was, yet still elegant and sophisticated, and you can truly taste the original flavour of the ingredients,” he says.
“We’re inspired by the methods and want to incorporate them in a way that makes sense for Malaysia.”
While he is aware that “most Chinese food in Malaysia has been dominated by Cantonese cuisine”, Wong also sees that the Malaysian Chinese experience isn’t a monolith.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Classic dishes, like coconut and silkie chicken soup, receive an injection of Penang produce with the inclusion of kulim (left), while 'lei cha' is reimagined with 'wosun', also known as celtuce. — Picture courtesy of Root House by gēn

It’s true across dialect groups, but also true within. He points out that the cuisine of Hakka communities in the North and the South of peninsular Malaysia varies, and so too does Fuzhou cuisine, depending on whether they settled in Sitiawan or Sibu.

“An example is lei cha. The herb mixture varies from place to place because some herbs, like mint, are more bitter in some places than others. We just try to make sure that we study it as widely as possible.”
Three months in, Wong says the response to Root House has split down the middle. “We get very polarising feedback,” he says.

“It’s not right or wrong; people here have been eating Chinese food for many years, so they’re used to one variation of Chinese food. It’s not the Chinese food they’re used to, but it’s what we are trying to introduce to Penang.”
Root House is part of the new wave of produce-driven, heritage-centred restaurants emerging across Malaysia, most of which are a hit with tourists.

In Penang, Wong’s other two restaurants arguably fit the bill. “gēn is still the mother. It all goes back to why I returned to Malaysia in the first place — I was interested in learning about Malaysian produce. Root House is the expression of my love for Chinese cooking,” he says.

“Here, we want to have more locals, because the idea is to introduce Chinese food done differently to them, to show that the cuisine can evolve. I understand preserving culture and tradition is very important. But we shouldn’t be stuck to it.

“We are ingredient-forward, but we don’t use premium ingredients in the way Chinese restaurants tend to. If we use an ingredient, we want to find a good reason for it. Some old-school chefs cannot accept it,” he says.
“But I believe there’s no right or wrong way; it’s just about what we want to achieve. For us, we remain produce-driven, same as at gēn, just expressed in a different way.”
What he does want is for people to keep talking after the plates are cleared. “We are very happy when we see diners linger at the table, deep in conversation about our dishes,” he says.
“It can be good or bad, discussing preferences, but that’s what we want to see. We don’t want people to just sit down, eat and then leave.”

There’s a process to it, he says, but the process cannot be the point. “Ultimately, making something good that makes your customer happy is what matters. If you’re just cooking for yourself, I don’t see the point.”

26d1fb1a935fcbe0: PETALING JAYA: Another DAP MP has joined in the call for the authorities to investigate a claim by PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang that a foreign power once offered assistance to the party to bring down the government.

Hadi had said at the PAS muktamar in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, yesterday that the offer of help to unseat the government was made at a meeting at the US embassy in 2014 during US president Barack Obama’s visit to Malaysia.
In a statement this morning, Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng asked if Hadi or other PAS leaders had informed the authorities about this earlier.
Lim described the claim as serious and said it must be supported by evidence.
He asked if the police had opened an investigation into the matter.
"The police must obtain statements from them and identify the American representative they were referring to.
"What exactly was offered? Was it merely a political conversation or a plan to unlawfully overthrow the government?" he said.
Last night, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer also called for an investigation into Hadi's claim, saying the public deserved to know what was discussed at the meeting.
Rayer said that if the allegation was true, it would constitute a matter of national security and sovereignty.
“What is even more disturbing is the apparent failure to report such an alleged meeting to the Malaysian authorities,” he wrote in a Facebook post.
In his speech, Hadi said PAS leaders Takiyuddin Hassan and Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar went to the US embassy for the meeting.
He claimed the US was “prepared to help topple the government”, but Takiyuddin and Samsuri were not swayed by the offer and remained firm in rejecting it.
