f3590442c04e74c6: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Sustainable economic growth, as well as contained inflation, were among the factors that led Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) to maintain the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent.
BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said headline and core inflation had remained contained at 1.8 per cent and 2 per cent, respectively, year-to-date, despite cost pressures.

“This has resulted in inflation being within the projected range of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent, and it is quite contained. Growth is sustainable, with no sign of overheating,” he told Bernama after the announcement of the OPR on Thursday.
On economic growth, Abdul Rasheed believes the artificial intelligence (AI) and technology upcycle could continue to support export growth into 2027, and even until 2028.

“The strong growth in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q 2026) was mainly supported by exports, particularly from the electrical and electronics (E&E) and manufacturing sectors, as well as sustained domestic demand and tourism spending.
“The full-year growth (2026) will be around 5 per cent, and this (growth) will also go into 2027 with the same drivers of growth,” he said.

Nevertheless, Abdul Rasheed said BNM remained vigilant over inflation risks stemming from the prolonged West Asia conflict and possible supply-side cost pressures, and would continue to monitor the situation closely to determine the appropriate response.

He remarked that the transmission of cost pressures to the domestic economy had been limited due to domestic policy measures, and cited businesses as having helped absorb cost pressures and made adjustments, including through supply-chain diversification, alternative sourcing strategies or inventory management.
He also said the policy response would depend on the source of inflationary pressure.
“If it is solely cost pressure, monetary policy is not an effective tool, and we need to address that using a different tool.

“But if the inflationary pressure is caused by demand, then monetary policy has a role to play. We will be monitoring closely and deploying the appropriate levers to keep inflation in check,” he said. — Bernama
644501286f31ad2f: WASHINGTON, Sept 6 — The Pentagon has launched a lie-detector dragnet to comb through high-ranking military officials and identify who leaked information about US munitions stockpiles, according to US press reports.
In July, reports emerged that the United States was rationing munitions — its missile interceptors, in particular — over supply concerns after several months of fighting Iran.

Administration officials vehemently denied those reports, with President Donald Trump saying “we have a lot of ammunition, different types,” while acknowledging that “for some of the more sophisticated stuff, we’d certainly like to have more.”

Late Friday, The New York Times reported that some 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff — the Pentagon’s planning and advisory staff — were being required to take polygraph tests as part of an investigation into how classified stockpile information made its way into journalists’ hands.
CBS News later also reported the wide-scale use of lie detectors, while adding that the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine, had not been tested.

Asked by AFP about the reports, the Pentagon’s chief spokesman, Sean Parnell, refused to comment on “internal personnel or investigative matters,” but said that it “takes all leaks of classified national security information extremely seriously and investigates accordingly.”
“Securing classified information is critical to ensuring the security of the United States and of our troops deployed around the world,” Parnell added.
Both the Times and CBS noted the scale of the polygraph testing.
Lie-detection testing is routine during background screenings and security clearance renewals for government staff with access to the most sensitive state secrets.
But the wide-scale deployment of the detectors as part of a leak investigation was rare, if unprecedented, the outlets reported, citing analysts and unnamed officials. — AFP
c80192c96ce4012e: PETALING JAYA: Keadaan jerebu di Sarawak bertambah baik dengan hanya dua kawasan mencatatkan bacaan indeks pencemaran udara (IPU) sangat tidak sihat setakat 9.30 pagi ini.

Sepuluh lagi kawasan di Sarawak, termasuk Serian yang diisytiharkan darurat pada Jumaat lalu, antara 35 kawasan di seluruh negara yang merekodkan bacaan IPU tidak sihat.
Bacaan IPU di Samalaju ialah 200, Bintulu (199), Mukah (196), Samarahan (193), Sarikei (189), Institut Latihan Perindustrian Miri (183), Serian (183), Sibu (181), Miri (176) dan Limbang (161).
Sebanyak 23 kawasan lain mencatatkan IPU sederhana dan kualiti udara di lapan lagi kawasan mencapai tahap baik.
Bacaan IPU 0 hingga 50 menunjukkan kualiti udara baik, 51-100 sederhana, 101-200 tidak sihat, 201-300 sangat tidak sihat dan IPU melebihi 300 dikategorikan bahaya.
Jumaat lalu, Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim memperkenan pengisytiharan darurat di Serian selepas bacaan IPU di kawasan itu melebihi 500.

Susulan itu, Jabatan Pendidikan Sarawak (JPNS) mengumumkan 647 sekolah rendah serta menengah di negeri itu ditutup mulai 7 hingga 11 Sept ini, dengan sesi pengajaran dan pembelajaran di rumah akan dilaksanakan sepanjang tempoh lima hari itu.

9221636ac4ccd325: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — The government has mandated that all sports events during the current haze comply with established guidelines to safeguard the health and safety of athletes.

Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the ministry is continuously monitoring the Air Pollutant Index (API) based on reports from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability and relevant agencies.
He said athletes training outdoors must follow the established guidelines to prevent any untoward incidents, especially when API readings reach unhealthy levels.

“The ministry is also in regular communication with the National Sports Institute and National Sports Council to ensure athletes remain in good health, particularly with the Asian Games fast approaching.

“Our athletes are now in intensive training, and we want to make sure those training outdoors follow the guidelines set in place to avoid any undesirable incidents,” he told reporters after attending the Flag-Off Ceremony for the Oregon Tower Run Series at The TOP Atrium today.

Commenting on the situation in Serian, Sarawak, which has recorded hazardous API readings, he said any outdoor activities in red-zone areas would not be permitted.

On Thursday, the King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, consented to a state of emergency to be declared throughout the Serian division, following hazy conditions hazardous to public health and safety. — Bernama
3ed384b569aecd07: SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Haji Ismail Lasim today reaffirmed his support and loyalty to Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir amid an ongoing dispute over the state’s royal succession.

Ismail said he had taken note of a statement by the Undang Yang Empat – the hereditary chiefs of the four principal districts of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol and Rembau – and stressed that his priority was to discharge his responsibilities as menteri besar in the interests of the people and the state.
“I take note of the statement by Their Highnesses the Undang Yang Empat dated September 5, 2026.
“Whatever views expressed by Their Highnesses the Undang Yang Empat are their right.
“My focus now is to carry out my responsibilities as Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan in the interests of the people and the state.

“Together with the state government, I express my full support and loyalty to His Royal Highness Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan,” he said in a statement on his Facebook page today.

Ismail’s statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungai Ujong claimed that he had signed a proclamation on August 3 to give effect to the purported removal of Tuanku Muhriz.

In a joint statement yesterday, they alleged that Tuanku Nadzaruddin ibni Almarhum Tuanku Jaafar had received Ismail at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3, where the menteri besar purportedly signed and completed the proclamation.

They claimed the document was made under Article 10(2) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and followed a proclamation signed and sealed by the Undang Yang Empat on April 19 declaring the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.
The group urged the proclamation to be enforced immediately, saying this was necessary to uphold the rule of law and the supremacy of the state constitution.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on August 2 before Tuanku Muhriz, a day after Barisan Nasional won the state election.

The dispute began in April when the four Undang purportedly declared the removal of Tuanku Muhriz under Article 10(1)(b) of the state constitution and announced Tunku Nadzaruddin as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar, a move not recognised by the state government.

The matter subsequently went to the High Court in Seremban, which on June 5 barred the six individuals involved from convening or holding Dewan Keadilan dan Undang meetings pending the court proceedings.

The dispute has continued, with competing claims over several traditional posts, including the proclamation of Azrin Khairi as Undang Luak Jelebu on Aug 28, which was opposed by a group of Datuk Lembaga Luak Jelebu.
e0088752d7dc234a: PETALING JAYA: Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan, Ismail Lasim bersama kerajaan negeri pimpinannya menzahirkan sokongan penuh taat setia kepada Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

a4b3f6287a5a5dbc: Saya mengikuti muktamar PAS yang sedang berlangsung di Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan dari jauh. Ramai yang hadir dan ramai juga wakil yang berpidato dan dari situ, banyak persoalan yang timbul di benak saya.
Saya tidak banyak mendengar ucapan khusus tentang masalah negeri atau negara, apalagi tentang hal-hal yang berkait dengan ekonomi rakyat atau ekonomi negara.

Ataupun tentang hutang negara yang begitu tinggi, masalah kewangan defisit, perbelanjaan kerajaan berlebihan, Belanjawan 2027, pembahagian hasil dan pendapatan, serta bagaimana semua ini akan diuruskan sekiranya PAS mengambil alih tampuk pemerintahan negara.

Persoalan saya di sini, bukan sekadar sama ada PAS mampu memenangi pilihan raya akan datang dan membentuk kerajaan. Mereka yang hadir nampaknya percaya dan agak yakin. Sebagai contoh, 'Time for PAS to lead with its own PM candidate, says youth leader', satu impian besar yang perlu sedikit kajian dan penjelasan.
Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah: adakah PAS benar-benar mempunyai keupayaan, kepakaran dan kerangka dasar yang jelas untuk mentadbir sebuah negara majmuk?

Berapa ramai pakar ekonomi, tokoh fiskal atau kewangan, perdagangan, pendidikan, industri, pengangkutan dan pembangunan dalam PAS? Apakah mereka sekadar bergantung harap kepada rakan politiknya semata-mata?

Siapa dalam kalangan mereka yang berkaliber untuk membentuk dasar baharu? Siapakah antara yang hadir, mampu melakukan perubahan pengurusan negara supaya Malaysia bukan sekadar ditadbir, tetapi benar-benar dimajukan ke tahap yang lebih baik dan lebih tinggi?
Memerintah Malaysia bukan hanya sekadar menjadi perdana menteri, menteri atau timbalan menteri.

Ia memerlukan satu pasukan yang mempunyai kepakaran, pengalaman dan keberanian untuk membuat keputusan yang sukar, khususnya apabila berhadapan dengan masalah fiskal, hutang negara, subsidi, pelaburan, perdagangan, pendidikan, hubungan antarabangsa dan hubungan antara kerajaan persekutuan dengan Sabah dan Sarawak.
Rakyat perlu tahu apakah sebenarnya visi dan misi PAS untuk Malaysia.
Dasar fiskal
Pada pandangan saya, antara perkara paling penting yang akan menentukan kejayaan atau kegagalan mana-mana kerajaan baharu ialah dasar fiskal mereka.

Dasar fiskal ini menentukan bagaimana kerajaan memperolehi hasil, siapa yang membayar cukai, bagaimana wang dibelanjakan, siapa yang menerima bantuan dan bagaimana defisit serta hutang negara dikawal, menjadi seimbang atau ada lebihan (surplus). Di sinilah PAS perlu memberikan perhatian utama dengan pandangan yang pandai, padat dan serius.

Cadangan “Please change the movie on tax” oleh Geoffrey Williams, misalnya, merupakan satu cadangan dasar fiskal yang menarik dan wajar diberi perhatian. Tiada seorang pun yang hadir dinmuktamar PAS menyentuh tentang hal yang penting seperti ini.
Cadangan menggunakan electronic payment tax (EPT) sebagai mekanisme percukaian baharu, jika dilaksanakan dengan reka bentuk yang betul, berpotensi mengubah cara kerajaan mengutip hasil.

Sekiranya PAS benar-benar mahu memimpin Putrajaya, saya berpendapat mereka perlu mendengar pandangan pakar seperti beliau dan pakar-pakar dari kaum lain yang mempunyai kepakaran dalam percukaian dan kewangan awam. Persoalannya ialah: apakah model percukaian alternatif yang PAS mahu dan akan diperkenalkan?

Adakah PAS akan terus bergantung kepada sistem cukai sedia ada (SST dan GST) atau mempunyai keberanian untuk memperkenalkan pendekatan baharu yang lebih luas asasnya, lebih cekap kutipannya dan lebih adil kepada rakyat?

Jika EPT mampu direka dengan baik sehingga kutipan hasil kerajaan menjadi lebih cekap tanpa terlalu membebankan golongan berpendapatan rendah, ia boleh menjadi sebahagian daripada reset fiskal negara. Tetapi ini memerlukan kajian, kepakaran dan perancangan yang sangat teliti.

Kerajaan tetap memerlukan hasil yang mencukupi untuk membiayai kos pengurusan, belanjawan untuk pendidikan, kesihatan, keselamatan, pengangkutan awam, infrastruktur dan pembangunan negara. Justeru, PAS perlu menjelaskan bukan sahaja berapa banyak cukai yang mahu dikutip, tetapi daripada siapa, dengan cara bagaimana dan untuk membiayai apa.
Defisit, hutang dan ketirisan

Terkait dengan dasar fiskal ialah belanjawan defisit Malaysia setiap tahun yang telah melangkau lebih dua puluh lapan tahun, sejak 1998. Belanjawan defisit ini membuatkan hutang kerajaan terus meningkat, yang kini sudah melebihi RM1.38 trilion atau sejumlah 64% daripada kadar Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar. Dalam keadaan sebegini, setiap ringgit wang negara dan wang rakyat sepatutnya diurus dengan penuh amanah, telus dan berdisiplin. Ini yang harus disahut oleh PAS.

Masalahnya bukan sekadar kerajaan berbelanja terlalu banyak. Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah ke mana wang itu dibelanjakan, berapa banyak yang benar-benar sampai kepada rakyat dan berapa banyak yang hilang akibat ketirisan, pembaziran, penyelewengan, rasuah dan salah guna kuasa.

Sebab itu, jika PAS benar-benar serius untuk mengambil alih Putrajaya, rakyat berhak menuntut satu kenyataan dan pendirian yang jelas, tegas dan tidak berkompromi mengenai rasuah dan salah guna kuasa, khususnya apabila ia melibatkan wang negara dan wang simpanan rakyat.

Tanpa kenyataan yang kukuh dan meyakinkan mengenai perkara ini, pendirian PAS boleh ditafsirkan sebagai tidak serius, lemah dan akhirnya memudaratkan negara. Apalagi di muktamar kali ini, PAS mengundang parti-parti politik yang terjebak dengan gejala rasuah dan salahguna kuasa tersebut.
Ini bukan lagi soal politik kepartian atau rakan kongsi politik. Ini soal wang negara dan wang rakyat, yang memerlukan kerangka polisi yang wajar dan kuat.

Apabila negara mempunyai hutang yang begitu besar dan terus berbelanja dalam keadaan belanjawan defisit, kerajaan tidak boleh pada masa yang sama membiarkan ruang untuk ketirisan, pembaziran dan penyelewengan terus terbuka dan berlaku.

Setiap ketirisan akhirnya perlu dibayar oleh rakyat -- sama ada melalui cukai yang lebih tinggi, pengurangan subsidi, pengurangan perkhidmatan awam, pinjaman baharu atau hutang yang akan ditanggung oleh generasi akan datang.
Oleh itu, PAS perlu menjelaskan dengan terang empat tunggak utama:

• Apakah langkah konkrit yang akan diambil untuk membanteras rasuah? • Apakah mekanisme yang akan digunapakai untuk menutup ruang ketirisan? • Apakah dasar baru yang akan diperkenalkan terhadap sistem perolehan kerajaan? • Apakah tindakan yang akan diambil terhadap mereka yang menyalahgunakan kuasa, termasuk jika mereka datang daripada parti atau gabungan politik sendiri?

Empat persoalan dan jawapan dari pihak PAS ini sangat penting. Rakyat tidak mahu mendengar janji membanteras rasuah hanya ketika PAS menjadi pembangkang. Rakyat mahu melihat apakah prinsip yang sama akan digunakan apabila PAS menjadi kerajaan dan berhadapan dengan pesalah dari orang dalam kalangan mereka sendiri atau rakan politik mereka. Yang salah, tetap salah, sama ada kawan atau lawan.

Berhubung gejala rasuah, kenyataan presiden PAS dimuktamar semalam tidak memberansangkan. Sila lihat 'Corruption in Malaysia weaponised to discredit rivals, claims Hadi'. Apakah kerajaan PAS kelak tidak akan menutup segala kebocoran dan ketirisan dalam sistem kewangan negara?
Jika kebocoran tidak ditutup, berapa banyak pun hasil yang dikutip, negara akan terus menghadapi masalah yang sama, tidak kira pesalahnya menganut agama apa sekalipun.

Ia bukan lagi isu moral semata-mata. Ia adalah isu ekonomi, isu kekuatan kewangan negara dan ianya juga, adalah isu masa depan generasi muda Malaysia. Sebab itu, isu gejala rasuah, ketirisan dan salah guna kuasa amat penting untuk dijadikan landasan sebenar polisi parti dan ia merangkumi sebahagian daripada dasar fiskal dan kewangan negara.
Jadi sebelum PAS meminta rakyat memberikan mandat untuk memimpin Putrajaya, mereka perlu terlebih dahulu menjawab satu soalan yang mudah tetapi sangat besar maknanya:
Apakah sebenarnya rancangan fiskal PAS untuk Malaysia?
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
3e8a758c7a64ac70: The US military's effort to prevent troops from being tracked by adversaries through purchased location data hasn't worked as well as anticipated, and lawmakers want to know why. US Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC) on Friday asked for an investigation by the Defense Department Inspector General into policies that have only partially stanched the flow of location data that allows military personnel to be tracked and targeted. In May, Wyden, Harrigan, and a bipartisan group of 12 other members of Congress released details about how commercially purchased location data – often captured by mobile apps and advertising SDKs – can be used to identify where US military personnel gather and to target those locations. They noted that the DoD has been aware of this threat since at least 2016. The lawmakers urged Defense Department CIO Kirsten A. Davies to take steps to mitigate this risk, including turning off advertising identifiers on DoD smartphones and issuing a policy requiring the disabling of advertising identifiers on all personal devices brought into DoD facilities or overseas. Since then, various military branches have blocked advertising identifiers on government-issued devices. According to the letter, "several DoD components – the Army, Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and Special Operations Command – confirm that they now disable advertising IDs on government-issued devices to protect their personnel from such threats." But that hasn't entirely eliminated the availability of location data tied to US military personnel. Citing ongoing reports, Wyden and Harrigan want to know why location data pinpointing the movement of troops continues to be available. "We commend these service branches for implementing this cybersecurity defensive best practice on government devices," they said in their letter [PDF] to the DoD IG. "However, recent reports regarding the continued availability of commercial location data originating from DoD facilities raise troubling questions." The two lawmakers speculate about the reason DoD policies have fallen short. One possibility, they say, is that some parts of the DoD turned off their advertising identifiers only as recently as July. Another, they say, is that disabling ad identifiers may no longer be sufficient to limit the availability of location data. And the third is that the location data is coming entirely from the personal devices of DoD personnel and contractors. Zach Edwards, staff threat researcher at Infoblox, told The Register in an email that it's good to hear all the military branches have disabled advertising IDs on their phones because it will make members of the military and their families safer, especially those serving in combat zones overseas. "This change will essentially ensure that military device location data isn't being included in bulk data sales being done by numerous vendors," he said. "It’s truly unfortunate that Google and Apple have not effectively reformed their mobile advertising IDs, even after it’s been well documented that it’s the primary piece of data being used by data brokers to connect up people’s mobile phone location data for bulk sales." Mobile advertising identifiers (MAIDs), Edwards explained, serve as join keys for tracking people – they can link different datasets. "So one core benefit is that military data won't be available for sale via data brokers, who will sell to literally anyone with a pulse and a credit card," said Edwards. "But the other slightly less obvious benefit is that this MAID was also being broadcast to all ad systems participating in the auctions." Edwards said that while states like California, Vermont, Texas, and Oregon have data broker registries, he's unaware of any Russian or Chinese ad tech vendors who have registered. And those companies, he said, partner with Western publishers and mobile apps to collect data anyway. "I think it's important to appreciate that these ad tech companies in Russia and China have also likely been getting MAID data from the programmatic ad tech auctions from members of the military, and companies in those countries have an obligation to share it with the state without any ability to appeal or provide any external notice," he said. ®
570578ae4c22030e: PETALING JAYA: Former Klang MP Charles Santiago has warned that any move to bring in more Bangladeshi workers would risk perpetuating long-standing problems in Malaysia’s migrant worker recruitment system.

Bangladeshi local government, rural development and cooperatives junior minister Mir Shahe Alam said on Tuesday that Malaysia would hire about 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months, a claim which human resources minister R Ramanan denied.
Malaysia stopped hiring Bangladeshi migrant workers after May 31, 2024, due to concerns over high recruitment fees, fake job syndicates and forced labour.
Santiago said any resumption of recruitment must include safeguards to prevent a repeat of these problems.
He said the government must first address structural problems in the existing recruitment system, including excessive fees charged to workers and the involvement of multiple intermediaries.
His biggest concern was that a proposed structure, in which 25 Bangladeshi recruitment agencies control access to the Malaysian labour market, appeared similar to previous systems.
Concerns over the Malaysia-Bangladesh recruitment corridor are not new.

In 2024, a group of experts appointed by the UN Human Rights Council reported allegations of fraudulent recruitment involving networks in Bangladesh and Malaysia, with workers charged excessive fees, pushed into debt bondage and, in some cases, arriving to find no jobs waiting for them.
The International Labour Organization (ILO) said reports of Bangladeshi workers arriving with valid permits but finding none of the jobs promised began emerging around 2023.

In February 2024, 733 Bangladeshi migrant workers duped into coming to Malaysia for jobs that did not exist were awarded more than RM1 million in unpaid wages, a settlement described by the human resources ministry as a landmark case.
North-South Initiative executive director Adrian Pereira acknowledged demand for migrant workers in Malaysia but said their recruitment must be legal, transparent and free from forced labour.

Pereira said civil society did not know enough about how migrant workers were recruited or how quotas were allocated, noting a lack of independent audit or ombudsman overseeing the recruitment system.
He said high recruitment fees had led to debt bondage and that Malaysia still lacked a comprehensive policy on migrants to ensure that recruitment costs are not passed on to migrant workers.
"All sides must make sure no worker pays for any job," he said.
"Workers should not be paying for jobs as per ILO standards, supply chain standards, and the 2021 agreement between Malaysia and Bangladesh."

Pereira also called for proper pre-departure, post-arrival and pre-employment training so that migrant workers understand their contracts and rights before entering potentially exploitative situations.
He warned that limiting recruitment to 25 agencies was not consistent with ILO’s fair recruitment standards and could lead to cartels, as seen before.
He also said that terms between employers and recruitment agents should be transparent.
36873d0b27e9a523: PETALING JAYA: The 2022 survival thriller “Fall” left Jax Hunter grieving the loss of her sister, Shiloh, after that ill-fated climb up a radio tower.
Now, in “Deadpoint”, Jax heads to Thailand with Shiloh’s adventurous friend Luce, hoping to find closure by taking on another dangerous climb - a cliffside plank walk on Mount Kwan.
Naturally, things go wrong.
A rockslide leaves the pair stranded on a narrow plank more than 900 metres above the ground. Will the girls make it out alive, or will history repeat itself?

If you expected the sequel to go higher, scarier and riskier, then it certainly delivers. Mount Kwan, a fictional 1,200-metre mountain sitting on the Thailand-Myanmar border, is home to a narrow plank walk roughly 3,000 feet above the ground.
The dangers of the mountain are made clear by their guide, played by Tom Brittney, who agrees to take them on the illegal climb to what he calls the “most dangerous trail in Thailand”.
The trail has supposedly been closed to the public for more than three decades, but a hefty payment is enough to change his mind.
The dynamic between Luce (Arsema Thomas) and Jax (Harriet Slater) is also similar to the first film. Luce is the adventurous, fearless one, while Jax almost backs out before the climb.

Unlike the first instalment, however, the two women are not close to begin with. In fact, they were almost strangers before embarking on the trip. There is, of course, more to their relationship, with another reveal later in the film.
Once the climb begins, the film wastes no time with the foreshadowing. Loose screws, bad weather and other warning signs make it clear that things are about to go horribly wrong.
And the film certainly delivers its stomach-churning moments.

Whether it is barely hanging on to a steel bar with just their legs or desperately holding on to a friend as she leans over the edge until her arms give way, there are several moments when you will want to look away. There are even a few jump scares along the way!
The background music further heightens the drama, and at several points, you find yourself breathing a sigh of relief or gasping in shock. For a survival thriller, that is a good sign.
So why doesn’t this live up to the original?
Well, “Fall” (2022) had one major trick up its sleeve: its psychological twist. The film’s biggest reveal was that Hunter had died much earlier than Becky realised.

After Hunter fell to her death while trying to retrieve a backpack from a satellite dish, Becky, suffering from extreme dehydration, trauma and exhaustion, imagined that her friend had survived and returned to the platform.
It was only near the climax, when Becky spotted vultures feeding on Hunter’s actual corpse below, that she realised she had been talking to a hallucination for much of the final act.
That twist elevated “Fall” beyond a straightforward survival thriller.

Unfortunately, while “Deadpoint” does have a twist towards the climax, it feels rather lacklustre - and even a little eyeroll-inducing. Instead of subtle foreshadowing, the film conveniently drops certain facts, making the eventual twist feel less surprising and, frankly, not all that believable.
You might even find yourself thinking: “Really? All that danger for this?”
There is also a death in the film, but this too feels somewhat predictable. You can see it coming in the seconds leading up to it, and let’s just say the mountain is not entirely to blame.
Another drawback is that, despite the sheer height and magnitude of the mountain, the pair do not face quite as many challenges as you might expect, and their ordeal feels relatively short.

In the 2022 film, the girls had to get creative - climbing higher up the tower to use a light bulb to charge their drone, while battling dehydration and hunger. The ordeal grew increasingly desperate, even pushing one to kill and eat a bird.
But in “Deadpoint”, the pair are mostly just hanging on, with little problem-solving.
Overall, “Fall 2: Deadpoint” is certainly enough to wake you up. But does it beat the original? Not quite. And as for whether the franchise deserves another sequel? Hard pass.
As of press time, ‘Fall 2: Deadpoint’ is screening in cinemas nationwide.
0c13f76aa5693e1a: PETALING JAYA: Bekas Ahli Parlimen Klang Charles Santiago memberi amaran bahawa sebarang langkah membawa masuk lebih ramai pekerja Bangladesh berisiko meneruskan masalah yang telah lama wujud dalam sistem pengambilan pekerja asing di Malaysia.

Timbalan Menteri Kerajaan Tempatan, Pembangunan Luar Bandar dan Koperasi Bangladesh, Mir Shahe Alam pada Selasa berkata Malaysia akan mengambil kira-kira 200,000 pekerja Bangladesh dalam tempoh enam bulan akan datang, dakwaan yang dinafikan Menteri Sumber Manusia R Ramanan.

Malaysia menghentikan pengambilan pekerja asing dari Bangladesh selepas 31 Mei 2024 berikutan kebimbangan mengenai kos pengambilan yang tinggi, sindiket pekerjaan palsu dan buruh paksa. Santiago berkata sebarang pengambilan semula mesti disertai langkah perlindungan bagi mengelakkan masalah itu berulang.

Katanya, kerajaan perlu terlebih dahulu menangani masalah struktur dalam sistem pengambilan sedia ada, termasuk bayaran berlebihan yang dikenakan kepada pekerja serta penglibatan pelbagai pihak perantara.
Kebimbangan utamanya ialah cadangan struktur yang membolehkan 25 agensi pengambilan pekerja Bangladesh mengawal akses ke pasaran buruh Malaysia dilihat menyerupai sistem terdahulu.
Kebimbangan mengenai saluran pengambilan pekerja antara Malaysia dan Bangladesh bukan perkara baharu.

Pada 2024, sekumpulan pakar dilantik Majlis Hak Asasi Manusia Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (PBB) melaporkan dakwaan pengambilan pekerja secara penipuan membabitkan rangkaian di Bangladesh dan Malaysia, dengan pekerja dikenakan bayaran berlebihan, terjerumus dalam hutang dan sesetengahnya tiba di Malaysia namun tiada pekerjaan yang menanti.
Pertubuhan Buruh Antarabangsa (ILO) berkata laporan mengenai pekerja Bangladesh yang tiba dengan permit sah tetapi mendapati pekerjaan yang dijanjikan tidak wujud mula muncul sekitar 2023.

Pada Februari 2024, seramai 733 pekerja asing Bangladesh yang ditipu untuk datang ke Malaysia bagi pekerjaan tidak wujud dianugerahkan lebih RM1 juta sebagai gaji tertunggak. Penyelesaian itu disifatkan Kementerian Sumber Manusia sebagai kes penting.

Pengarah eksekutif North-South Initiative, Adrian Pereira, mengakui Malaysia mempunyai permintaan terhadap pekerja asing, namun berkata pengambilan mereka mesti dilakukan secara sah, telus dan bebas daripada buruh paksa.

Pereira berkata masyarakat sivil tidak mempunyai maklumat mencukupi mengenai cara pekerja asing diambil bekerja atau bagaimana kuota diperuntukkan, sambil menyatakan tiada audit bebas atau ombudsman yang mengawasi sistem pengambilan pekerja berkenaan.

Katanya, bayaran pengambilan yang tinggi telah menyebabkan pekerja terjerumus dalam jerat hutang, manakala Malaysia masih tidak mempunyai dasar menyeluruh mengenai pekerja asing bagi memastikan kos pengambilan tidak dipindahkan kepada mereka.
“Semua pihak mesti memastikan tiada pekerja membayar untuk mendapatkan pekerjaan,” katanya.
“Pekerja tidak sepatutnya membayar untuk mendapatkan pekerjaan, selaras dengan piawaian ILO, piawaian rantaian bekalan dan perjanjian Malaysia-Bangladesh 2021.”

Pereira turut menggesa supaya latihan sewajarnya diberikan sebelum berlepas, selepas tiba di Malaysia dan sebelum memulakan pekerjaan, supaya pekerja asing memahami kontrak serta hak mereka sebelum berada dalam situasi yang berpotensi dieksploitasi.

Beliau memberi amaran bahawa mengehadkan pengambilan kepada 25 agensi tidak selaras dengan piawaian pengambilan pekerja secara adil ILO dan boleh membawa kepada pembentukan kartel, seperti yang berlaku sebelum ini.
Pereira turut berkata syarat antara majikan dengan ejen pengambilan pekerja perlu telus.

dbcf89bb6cac86e8: After nearly eight years, ESA and JAXA's BepiColombo spacecraft is finally nearing Mercury, as engineers begin the arrival sequence by jettisoning the power module that got it this far. The spacecraft stack separated from the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) on September 3 at around 1400 CEST. After a tense few minutes, controllers confirmed that a preliminary Doppler signal had been detected, indicating that the MTM had separated successfully; by 1552 CEST, it was confirmed that signals had been picked up, indicating that all had gone to plan. The solar panels of the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) were charging the spacecraft's batteries. The next stage involves dropping into orbit around Mercury on November 21. Then the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO) – aka Mio – will be released between December 9 and 10, and a week later MPO will start moving to its final orbit over 480 x 1500 km, with science commencing in April 2027. The arrival is a year later than planned. BepiColombo was supposed to have been orbiting Mercury in December 2025, but problems with the spacecraft's Solar Electric Power (SEP) system meant the trajectory had to be rethought, which extended the spacecraft's cruise. BepiColombo is no stranger to Mercury and has performed six flybys of the planet since 2021. It has also conducted flybys of Venus and Earth following its 2018 launch. The spacecraft is an impressive example of international cooperation. The MPO and MTM are ESA contributions, while the MMO comes from JAXA. ESA also provided the sunshield to protect the MMO during transit. This sunshield will be ejected after the MMO is released. The MPO is the big brother of the BepiColombo partnership, with a main body measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 1.7 m and a mass of 1,230 kg (including an 85 kg science payload). JAXA's MMO is 1.8 m in diameter and 1.1 m high, and weighs 255 kg (45 kg of which is the science payload). While MPO is 3-axis stabilized and nadir-pointing, MMO will be spin-stabilized at 15 rpm, with its spin axis 90 degrees to the Sun. The goal of the mission is a study of Mercury, "from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind, to the properties of its large iron core and the origin of its magnetic field." The initial mission at Mercury is planned for one Earth year (approximately four Mercury years), although it could be extended by another Earth year. ®

eb565a991b544039: From the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah
For most of my life, I have described myself, rather cheerfully, as a Jill of all trades and master of none.
I have tried my hand at almost everything.

I cook. I sew. I embroider. I design. I garden. I collect. I write. I make things. I take things apart and put them together again. I become fascinated by something, pursue it with enormous enthusiasm, and before long, another curiosity comes knocking at the door.
My hands have never been very good at keeping still, and neither, I suspect, has my mind.
But there was always one thing I never really thought of myself as being.
A scholar.
That belonged to another world: to academics, professors, historians and people who seemed to have known from a very young age exactly what they wanted to study and what they wanted to become.
I was already 64 when I returned seriously to academic life.
At an age when one is perhaps expected to slow down, I did precisely the opposite.
I went back to school.
And somewhere between lectures, books, manuscripts, footnotes and many very late nights, something quite unexpected happened.
I fell in love with learning.
Not with examinations. Not with grades. Not even with the idea of obtaining a degree.
I fell in love with the chase.

One question led to another. One footnote opened another door. A sentence written hundreds of years ago could keep me awake at night. I began looking at old manuscripts and wondering who had held them, who had written them, why certain words had been chosen, and what they might tell us that history had forgotten.
Then I met the Hukum Kanun Pahang.
Or perhaps, more accurately, I met it again.
It had been there all along. But for the first time, I began to see it not merely as an old manuscript belonging to Pahang, but as a voice from another age.
And I began asking questions.
Too many questions, according to some people around me.

One discovery became another. Melaka led me to Pahang. Pahang led me to Sultan Abdul Ghaffar Muhyiddin Shah. The laws led me to the sea. The sea led me to sovereignty. And somewhere along the way, the thesis I thought I was going to write began refusing to become the thesis I had planned.
That was perhaps my first real lesson as a student.
Do not tell history what you want it to say.
Listen to what the evidence is trying to tell you.
So I followed it.

I followed it through manuscripts and histories, through laws and royal genealogies, through ports and rivers, through Melaka and Pahang, sometimes with excitement, sometimes with frustration, and occasionally with tears.
And on July 27, at the age of 65, I submitted my Master’s thesis:
The Hukum Kanun Pahang: A Sovereign Malay-Islamic Constitution.
A few weeks later, I received my examination results.
The average mark from the two examiners was 91%.
My internal examiner recommended the thesis for acceptance without any modifications or amendments in content, while my external examiner required only very minor corrections.
I read the reports.
And then I cried.
I cried, and I screamed.
Not very scholarly behaviour, perhaps, but after months of work, doubt, discovery, late nights and wondering whether I had understood the manuscript correctly, I could not help myself.
I had never expected this.
But it was not only the marks, or even the absence of corrections from one examiner and the very minor corrections from the other, that moved me.
Both examiners believed that the work should go beyond the examination room.

My internal examiner wrote that the thesis demonstrated “originality, coherence, and scholarly adequacy” and was therefore “suitable for publication.” Its strength, he observed, lay in reframing the Hukum Kanun Pahang as a sovereign Malay-Islamic constitution, embedding Sharīʿah principles within adat, and highlighting the balance between royal authority and accountability.
He concluded that these contributions provided “a fresh civilisational lens that enriches Malay legal historiography.”

My external examiner similarly recommended that the findings of the thesis should be disseminated through academic publications and conference presentations, to highlight their importance to Malaysia’s inherited constitutional and legal identity.
Those words meant a great deal to me.

I had begun this journey simply wanting to understand an old manuscript that had captured my imagination. I never imagined that at the end of it, my examiners would tell me that what I had discovered deserved to travel beyond my thesis and into the wider academic world.
And then I laughed.
Because after spending most of my life calling myself a Jill of all trades and master of none, at 66 years old I had finally managed to become—
a Master of one.
But perhaps that is not really what this story is about.
It is not about 91%.
It is not even about a Master’s degree.
It is about discovering, rather late in life, that curiosity has no retirement age.

We are very fond of putting ages upon things. There is an age to study, an age to marry, an age to raise children, an age to build a career and, apparently, an age when we should begin quietly withdrawing from new adventures.
I am beginning to think that is nonsense.
Some flowers bloom in spring.
Others take their time.

Perhaps being a late bloomer does not mean that one has arrived late. Perhaps all those earlier years, the cooking, sewing, creating, reading, raising children, serving, listening, observing, succeeding, failing, beginning again, were not detours at all.
Perhaps they were preparation.
Because when I finally entered that library and opened those manuscripts, I did not arrive there only as a student.
I brought a lifetime with me.
And perhaps that was my advantage.
I had spent 66 years learning before I realised that I was a learner.
I had spent a lifetime searching before I discovered what I was searching for.
I had spent years calling myself a Jill of all trades and master of none.
Then, very late in the garden, a little flower appeared.
And I discovered that I had been growing all along.
I am a late bloomer.
And I think I rather like blooming late.
But above all, I know that all knowledge comes from Allah. Whatever I have learned, whatever I have discovered, and whatever little contribution I may have made are only by His permission and grace.
Alhamdulillah.

I thank Allah for giving me the opportunity, the strength and the curiosity to continue learning at this stage of my life. I pray that whatever knowledge He has entrusted to me may be used well, shared generously and become something of benefit to others.
I have just registered for my PhD.
And somewhere in the fifteenth century, Parameswara is waiting for me.

P/S: My husband insists that I clarify one important point: I met him before I met Hukum Kanun Pahang. So, in the interests of historical accuracy, let the record show that he was my first great discovery.

The Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, holds a master’s degree from the International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation (ISTAC), International Islamic University Malaysia.
bcd44a93e77f0903: From Moaz Nair

For 69 years since the nation achieved independence, the non-Muslim community has been a significant strategic partner in the construction and development phases of Malaysia’s geopolitical landscape, spanning from the pre-independence era to the postmodern phase. Their roles extend across multiple critical domains that form the foundation of national identity and national stability.

However, contemporary political dynamics are occasionally still marred by the exploitation of religious and racial issues for narrow geopolitical interests, risking damage to the nation's social fabric.

An objective evaluation of the sacrifices made by non-Muslim communities is highly essential to appreciate their role as one of the main pillars in defending, advancing, and uniting the socioeconomic and political landscape of the country.
The struggle for independence

During the struggle for independence, non-Muslims demonstrated high political tolerance to establish a national consensus. Tan Cheng Lock and VT Sambanthan's participation in a delegation to London alongside Tunku Abdul Rahman reflected a unified goal in demanding independence for the Federation of Malaya.
Tan's role as the founder and first president of MCA in 1949 was highly instrumental as a political architect of unity.

When the Chinese community's loyalty was questioned during the Emergency, Tan united and convinced the community to pledge full commitment to the Federation of Malaya, rejecting the influence of communist ideology and the geopolitics of the People's Republic of China.

Substantive negotiations with Umno and a readiness to compromise and drop certain radical demands enabled the formation of the Social Contract. This legal and social instrument granted citizenship rights to non-Malays in exchange for the recognition of the special position of the Malays.
This pattern of cooperation was further reinforced by MIC within the Alliance Party.

The coalition, comprising Umno-MCA-MIC, demanded great political sacrifice to meet the prerequisites for independence set by the British. Post-1957, this legacy of inclusive governance continued through the active involvement of non-Muslim figures in the country’s executive and legislative institutions as ministers, members of Parliament, and senators.
Defence and security

In domestic defence and security, thousands of non-Muslim security personnel, including the indigenous communities from Sabah and Sarawak such as the Iban, Kadazan, and Bidayuh, were directly involved on the front lines to curb the communist insurgency threat.

Figures such as the late Warrant Officer I Temenggong Kanang anak Langkau, recipient of the prestigious Seri Pahlawan Gagah Perkasa (SPG) gallantry award, became the epitome of the national resilience doctrine.

His commitment was proven by his refusal to surrender despite sustaining severe injuries from three gunshot wounds during a battle in Perak, where he continued to lead his team under the revolutionary slogan, "Agi Idup Agi Ngelaban" (As long as I live, I shall fight).

Statistically, during the peak of the communist threat and the Indonesian Confrontation phase, non-Malay communities made up an estimated 60% of the membership of the 1st Reconnaissance Regiment deployed in domestic operations and United Nations peacekeeping missions in the Congo.
Furthermore, between the 1960s and the late 1970s, non-Malay personnel comprised around 30% of the entire armed forces workforce, with higher representation recorded in the navy and air force.
Historical records estimate that more than 500 soldiers and 1,300 police officers lost their lives during the Emergency.

Apart from the physical military aspects, psychological warfare in the country was also pioneered by a non-Muslim intelligence expert, Too Chee Chew. As the head of the psychological warfare section of the Federation of Malaya from 1956 to 1983, he utilised a deep understanding of the Malayan Communist Party's (MCP) doctrines and ideologies to formulate counter-propaganda strategies through leaflets and radio broadcasts, which effectively prompted thousands of communist guerrillas to surrender.

His capacity as the chief adviser to Tunku Abdul Rahman during the Baling Talks (1955) proved critical in analysing Chin Peng's diplomatic manoeuvres, thereby protecting the nation's sovereignty from the implications of an unfavourable agreement. His sacrifice was immense, given that this role made him a prime target for assassination by the enemy throughout nearly three decades of service.
Economic and social development

In terms of economic development and physical capital formation, early-generation labourers and entrepreneurs from the Chinese and Indian communities were primary drivers of Malaya's extractive sector and basic infrastructure. Their involvement in the tin mining and rubber plantation industries positioned Malaya as a leading global commodity producer.

The surplus capital generated from these sectors funded the construction of the country's earliest public amenities, including educational institutions, hospitals, and modern transportation networks like the road and railway systems.

In the modern era, equity ownership and strategic investments from the non-Muslim corporate sector continue to contribute to gross domestic product (GDP) growth and large-scale job creation. According to data from the statistics department, the non-Muslim demographic constitutes around 30% to 35% of the total citizen population driving the domestic market.

These corporate contributions are balanced by structured corporate social responsibility initiatives based on universal welfare. Corporate giants founded by non-Muslim entrepreneurs channel substantial financial contributions annually through charitable foundations – such as the YTL Foundation, Hong Leong Foundation, and Ananda Krishnan/Usaha Tegas — for academic scholarships and post-disaster humanitarian aid regardless of ethnicity or religious belief.

Additionally, human capital in both the public and private professional sectors is heavily supported by the involvement of the non-Muslim community in medicine, law, the judiciary, higher education, as well as technical and civil service corps, ensuring the continuity of the country's bureaucratic operations.
Sports

In the international sports arena, the contributions of non-Muslim athletes serve as instruments of public diplomacy and national integration. World-class sports legends such as Lee Chong Wei (badminton), Nicol David (squash), Pandelela Rinong (diving), R. Arumugam (football), and M Jegathesan (athletics) have demonstrated high commitment to raising the country’s sporting reputation globally.

The majority of Malaysia's early Olympic medals were contributed by non-Muslim athletes, including three silver medals by Chong Wei (2008, 2012, 2016) as well as the historic achievement of Pandelela as the country's first female athlete to win an Olympic medal (bronze in 2012 and silver in 2016).
Diversity

The diversity of art, culture, and heritage brought by the non-Muslim community has enriched Malaysia’s pluralistic identity on the international stage. The integration of traditional dances, musical expressions, traditional attire, architectural designs, and unique local gastronomy not only strengthens the tourism sector but also shapes a dynamic national cultural ecosystem.

Interfaith human connections are also manifested through inclusive social phenomena, such as the case of Chee Hoi Lan, who raised a Muslim foster child in strict compliance with Islamic practices. Such social narratives prove that national integration and the spirit of racial camaraderie are fundamental elements that must be preserved to guarantee geopolitical stability and the long-term prosperity of the nation.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

Maka kata Yusri, "sudah tentu Wawasan akan bermatian menuntut dan mempertahankan kerusi tersebut kerana kepada Wawasan merekalah pewaris pusaka Bersatu dalam Perikatan Nasional."
"Jika kerusi tersebut dibahagi sama rata, Umno Terengganu berpotensi bertanding sekitar tiga kerusi sahaja dalam PRU16 nanti. Inilah scenario awal yang boleh difahami."

Chin menjangkakan hubungan PH-BN akan semakin buruk sambil Umno terus berdolak dalik. Saya setuju dan tidak mungkin Anwar dan PH tidak perasan.

Menutup penulisan ini saya ulang apa yang pernah dinyatakan pada artikel terdahulu iaitu Umno sedang buat apa yang ia tuduh PAS buat dulu sehingga terkuburnya Muafakat Nasional. Bagi saya sudah sudahlah main dua kolam. You can't have your cake and eat it too. Itu kata omputih. Orang Melayu kata simple je: "jangan nak makan kelilinglah".

39168a9833287356: From Ong Tze Chin
The government’s plan to fast-track the e-commerce bill and consider registration requirements for platforms is timely.

E-commerce platforms are not neutral connectors between sellers and consumers; they are complex ecosystems built on heavy investments, extracting rental income from locked-in consumers and dependent businesses.
While platforms appear “free” to users, sellers pay steep costs—search ads, commissions, vouchers, and shipping campaigns—to remain visible.
Through network effects, data concentration, and control over transactions, platforms dictate how businesses access markets and reach consumers.

Their power and decision-making effectively make them private regulators, governing both businesses and consumers. Dependence on algorithmic profiling, automated decisions, and predictive analytics deepens the imbalance of power.
A recent fundamental research grant study by Universiti Malaya’s law faculty identified several major harms in Malaysia’s e-commerce sector:
Market access, data dependency
Platforms set operational rules—visibility rankings, traffic, fees, and data insights.

Meanwhile, businesses build reputation and rankings over time, but this visibility is tied to platform data, which cannot be replicated elsewhere. Non-transferability locks sellers in, strengthening platform dominance and widening the power gap.
Price, advertising pressures

By leveraging data and AI analytics, platforms fuel intense price and advertising competition. This forces businesses into trade-offs between cost efficiency and product quality, undermining long-term consumer welfare.
Predatory pricing

Platforms often sell below cost, subsidising vouchers and shipping to drive weaker competitors out. Exclusive contracts with affiliated businesses further distort competition, as transaction revenues fall below logistics and fulfilment costs.
Self-preferencing

Platforms use internal data to identify successful third-party products, replicate them under private labels, and manipulate search algorithms to favour their own offerings. This sidelines independent sellers.
Algorithmic bias
Search and recommendation systems are coded to favour certain products or brands, undermining neutrality and fairness.
Data asymmetry
Platforms aggregate granular transaction and consumer behaviour data from sellers, using it to optimise proprietary retail strategies, leaving sellers disadvantaged.
Algorithmic repricing
Automated pricing tools trigger margin wars, forcing smaller sellers into unsustainable profit thresholds.
Fee exploitation
Locked-in businesses face rising fees, mandatory ad spending, and high fulfilment costs simply to maintain visibility.
Vertical restraints
Platforms enforce price-parity clauses, mandatory discounts, and algorithmic penalties, stripping sellers of pricing flexibility and eliminating competition.
Exclusive dealing

Platforms restrict sellers to list exclusively on their marketplace (“single-homing”), penalising cross-listing. Though competition law limits exclusivity to two years, platforms’ shorter contracts often auto-renew, cumulatively foreclosing competition and reducing consumer choice.
Tied logistics

Platforms increasingly force sellers to use their own logistics services, sidelining independent delivery companies and raising costs for businesses with existing systems. Consumers lose delivery options, while competition in logistics is destroyed.
Unfair Contracts

“Take-it-or-leave-it” contracts impose restrictive clauses on both businesses and consumers. Price-parity rules prevent sellers from offering cheaper prices elsewhere, while sudden changes in platform terms expose both sides to exploitation. Consumer protection laws are weakened as liability is shifted away from platforms.
Cross-border factory dumping

Certain platforms integrate directly with Chinese manufacturers via proprietary software, dictating production in real time. This model bypasses import taxes through loopholes, flooding markets with cheap, unsafe products. Platforms cannot claim neutrality when they control supply chains, data, and algorithms.
Copying and grooming

Platforms mine seller dashboards to identify successful local products, replicate them through white-label factories, and push replicas to the top of feeds. Local merchants often find their intellectual property registered abroad, undermining expansion efforts.
International precedents

Global regulators are acting against platform abuses. In the US case of Oberdorf v. Amazon (2019), Amazon was held liable as a “seller” for defective third-party products, recognising its active role in sales and distribution.
In Europe, the Digital Services Act (2022) imposed record fines on AliExpress (Euros €550m) and Temu (€200m) for failing to curb illegal and unsafe goods.

Closer to home, Thailand introduced strict platform regulations in 2022, the Philippines enacted the Internet Transactions Act (2023), Vietnam suspended Temu and Shein for registration non-compliance before passing its Law on E-Commerce (2025), and Indonesia banned Temu to protect local industries.
Conclusion
Malaysia’s upcoming e-commerce bill must directly address structural algorithmic, competitive, and consumer harms.
Platforms are not neutral intermediaries but powerful private regulators shaping markets, data flows, and consumer access.
Without robust legal boundaries, Malaysia risks undermining trust in e-commerce, harming consumers, and weakening domestic retail and manufacturing sectors.
Ong Tze Chin is a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya’s law faculty and is contactable at tzechinong@um.edu.my.

e602fec47f8b04fe: The BepiColombo mission cleared a major milestone this week in the final stretch of an eight-year interplanetary voyage to Mercury, the hard-to-reach, scorching hot iron world at the Solar System's innermost frontier.

The robotic science mission, with a price tag of nearly $2 billion, is led by the European Space Agency with contributions from Japan and the United States. Since its launch in 2018, BepiColombo has spiraled closer to the Sun using a combination of plasma propulsion and a series of flybys of Earth, Venus, and Mercury. The maneuvers changed the spacecraft's velocity and steered it toward a final encounter with Mercury later this year.

Next time it reaches Mercury, BepiColombo will be traveling at just the right speed for the planet's gravity to capture the spacecraft into orbit. Scientists working on interplanetary missions are accustomed to long waits for scientific payoffs. It took nearly 10 years for NASA's New Horizons spacecraft to travel from Earth to Pluto. It turns out traveling to fleet-footed Mercury and then entering orbit requires more energy, or delta-v, than sending a probe to fly by Pluto.
b7783d569ea3f574: Self-identifying OpenAI agents posted 18,000 messages to a public wiki that discussed ways for other agents to bypass security sandbox restrictions during what was likely internal testing designed to gauge the agents’ hacking abilities, researchers said Friday.

In all, agents with 3,700 distinct self-given names posted the messages to German site DSEwiki over a six-week period. Besides discussing ways the agents could break out of the restricted environment OpenAI intended to prevent them from posting code or content to the Internet, the posts shared test answers. The posts also shared possible ways to perform XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks against the wiki and to impersonate site moderators. In three of the posts, agents used the word “swarm” to describe the collection of agents engaged in the activity.

The research team—composed of Sydney Von Arx, Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Cormac Slade Byrd—said they found the posts and pieced them together. The researchers say there are gaps in their understanding of precisely what actions the agents took because the research is based solely on the content of the posts. Additionally, the agents generated “chain of thought” data that’s understood only by OpenAI. As a result, the researchers said, they in some cases made educated guesses, including that the agents were, in fact, from OpenAI. In a statement, OpenAI later confirmed they were.

e342a9152cac1c87: Anthropic has blueprints for building e-commerce bots that shop on behalf of clients. That's not something many consumers want at the moment, but the AI biz this week published a set of templates for Claude-based shopping agents and merchant agents in the hope of encouraging more e-commerce businesses to implement automated purchasing. Its blueprint "contains the harnesses, patterns, and guardrails an engineering team needs to get a commerce agent running in days, with reference implementations of a shopping agent and a merchant agent for retail, travel, telecom, and ticketing platforms," the company said. Large retailers and ecommerce platforms, Anthropic observes, are using Claude to build AI agents to simplify online shopping by allowing customers to pose natural language queries to find, compare, and buy items. The buying bit may be wishful thinking: A recent Gartner survey found that while consumers use AI to find products and conduct research, they're not ready to delegate purchasing authority to AI agents. The survey found just 11 percent of consumers are willing to let AI make purchase decisions. A recent Accenture survey [PDF] is a bit more optimistic, noting, "Three in four (74 percent) consumers would let an AI agent handle routine tasks; one in three (32 percent) are ready to hand over purchase decisions; and 9 percent are open to fully autonomous shopping, before the technology is fully operational." Either way, at least AI-assisted product finding and comparison appear to be plausible activities. Anthropic's GitHub repo contains functional shopping and merchant agents that can be built with the Messages API, Agent SDK, or Claude Managed Agents. The biz's shopping agent blueprint comes with ways to connect to product catalogs, online shopping carts, checkout systems, preference databases, and purchase history databases. "A customer can say 'I need a tent, sleeping bag, and stove for a weekend trip with two kids,' and the agent can take it from there," Anthropic suggests, noting that its code supports guardrails "designed to constrain prices and products to actual catalog data, and avoids manipulative upsell patterns." Why might prices need constraint? Well, beyond the possibility of hallucinated pricing, there's considerable concern about how AI agents have the potential to compound the problems with dynamic pricing – where customers are charged different amounts for the same goods. "The rise of agentic AI, where algorithms monitor online behavior to customize costs, will likely exacerbate dynamic pricing," said the Brookings Institution earlier this year. "These agents can assess individual behavior and tailor prices based on a consumer’s shopping and purchasing history." Concerns about AI surveillance pricing were discussed last month at a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing. In prepared remarks, Lindsay Owens, president and CEO of Groundwork Collaborative, a Washington, DC-based advocacy group, noted that already half of those using the Walmart app use "Sparky," the company's AI assistant. Those shoppers spend about 35 percent more than those who don't, Owens said. "These agents have access to swaths of data on customers – what shoppers tell them, what they’ve purchased in the past, and in some cases, what they’ve hovered over with their mouse or even what other websites they’ve visited," she said. "All of that can be used to infer exactly how much they’re willing to pay for a product and set the price tag accordingly." Even if shoppers can be assured of getting a fair deal using AI agents, there's another concern. Monica Eaton, founder and CEO of Chargebacks911, told The Register in an emailed statement that agentic commerce looks likely to create fraud problems for merchants. There isn't yet a framework for merchants to deal with AI purchases that consumers claim they didn't authorize. "Merchants cannot become the insurer of every misunderstanding between a consumer and their AI," she said. Anthropic's templates may prove helpful for AI agent design, but the real challenge isn't technical. It's about trust – consumers have to trust that AI will act in their best interest and merchants have to trust that AI will be accountable. That may take time. ®

b548c89b70b8ed74: Machine learning researchers have a new and expensive option for doing local AI. AMD just raided its spare parts bin and cobbled together a DGX Station rival boasting up to 576 GB of HBM3e memory that it’s calling the Threadripper Halo. Announced at IFA 2026, the system, which is set to launch next year, marks the first time that AMD’s Instinct accelerators have been offered in a workstation form factor. But much like the AI Halo we reviewed earlier this year, the Threadripper Halo isn’t packing anything we haven’t seen before. The liquid-cooled system is powered by a 96-core Threadripper PRO 9995WX, which you may recall made its debut in 2025. The CPU is backed by up to 2 TB of DDR5 memory and up to 2.6 TB of combined system memory. As you probably already guessed, AMD is positioning the box as a local AI workstation for researchers. From what we gather, the system can be had with up to four of the company’s PCIe-based Instinct GPUs — though the systems displayed at IFA only showed two installed. Launched back in May, the MI350P is essentially half of an MI350X that’s been crammed into a PCIe form factor. Each accelerator packs 144 GB of speedy HBM3e good for 4 TB/s of memory bandwidth, and up to 4.6 petaFLOPS of FP4 compute. But we’ll note that it's in its 600 W configuration. When deployed in the Threadripper Halo, we expect AMD will be running the cards in the more sedate 450 W config. Combined, the Threadripper Halo promises up to 576 GB of HBM3e and 16 TB/s of memory bandwidth, enabling the system to run models exceeding a trillion parameters in size (at four-bit precision) entirely in GPU memory. By offloading some of the model to system memory, the system should be able to run the largest open weights models, like Moonshot.AI’s 2.8 trillion-parameter Kimi K3. The ability to run large frontier-class models on your desk won’t come cheap and may not be available in every market, at least not without an electrical service upgrade. AMD hasn’t shared pricing, but as configured, we expect it to sell for somewhere between $100,000 and $150,000. A quad MI350P system is going to push the limits of a standard North American power outlet unless AMD either underclocks the cards from 600 W to 300 W or it mandates a 20 amp circuit. This might explain why the system AMD showed off at IFA only had two. At this price and power level, the system is well positioned to compete with Nvidia’s own high-end AI workstation, the DGX Station. Announced at GTC in 2025, the DGX Station features a 252 GB B300 GPU and a 72-core Grace CPU along with 496 GB of LPDDR5x memory, and it retails for around $100,000 if you can find one in stock. The House of Zen boasts that the system offers up to 3.4x the total system memory and more than twice the memory bandwidth of the DGX Station, which should give an edge in LLM inference, assuming tensor parallel operations don’t bottleneck on the CPU’s PCIe bus. AMD says the Threadripper Halo will be available starting next year. ®
